Provs., Nigeria, May-Dec., 1921; ag. res., Sokoto Prov., Apr. to May, 1922; lieut.-gov., N. Provs., Nigeria, May, 1925; gov., Gambia, 1930.

PALMER, RICHARD HENRY, B.A. (Oxon.).—B. 1881; ed. St. Cuthbert's Schl., Worksop, and Keble Coll., Oxford; Cape civ. serv., 1903; clk., dist. admstve., N.W. Rhodesia, Oct., 1906; astt. native commnr., May, 1908; native commnr., N. Rhodesia, Sept., 1911; ag. astt. mag., Mar., 1915; astt. mag., Apr., 1916; ag. res. mag., Barotse dist. in 1924 and 1926; mag., July, 1927; J.P.; prov. commnr., Apr., 1929; senr. prov. commnr., 1932.

PAMELLONE, ARMAND JOSEPH, M.B., Ch.B. Edin.—B. 1879; entd. med. serv., Trinidad, 1st Feb., 1906; dist. med. offr., 1st Aug., 1913.

PANES, JOHN NELSON.—B. 1888; ed. Dean Close Schl. and Hertford Coll., Oxford (M.A. hon.); mast., King Edward VI's Schl., Norwich, 1914-22; astt. mast., King's Coll., Lagos, Nigeria, 1922; supt., educn., S.P., Nigeria, 1925; ag. ch. inspr., educn., 1930-31; prin., King's Coll., Lagos, 1931.

PANET, LIEUT.-COL. CHARLES LOUIS.—B. 1870; ed. Ottawa Univ.; ent. civ. serv., Canada, 1889; sec., Canadian defence comte., 1898; priv. sec. to late Sir F. W. Borden, min. of militia and defence, 1904-12; sec., dept. of militia and defence from 1907; pres. bd. of enquiry, re claims of applicants for the fenian raid volunteer bounty, 1912-15; pres. of pensions and claims bd.; ment. in desp. for serv. rendered in Can., 1914-1918.

PAPAFIO, M.K.Q.—Ed. Accra Grammar Schl. and in England; 6th grade teacher, 1911; 5th grade do., 1912; 2nd cls. do., 1919; 1st cls. do., 1920; headmistress, 1921.

PAPATETROU, ANTONI, M.B.E. (1927).—B. 1878; clk., land regiarn. and survey dept., Cyprus, Oct., 1903; inspr., land regiarn. and survey dept., Apr., 1919; astt. regir.-gen., Mar., 1927; title altered to astt. dir., land regiarn. and surveys, July, 1927; ag. dir., land regiarn. and surveys for various periods, 1928-32.

PARHAM, ARTHUR DOUGLAS, F.R.I.B.A., F.S.I., Chartered Archt. and Quantity Surv., mem., Town Planning Inst.—B. 1890; ed. King's Coll., London; temp. architectural astt., P.W.D., Ceylon, 1915; 1st astt. archt., 1918; ag. ch. archt. in 1919, 1923, 1925, 1927 and 1929; astt., town planning divn., Miny. of Health, 1926.

PARISH, GODFREY CHARLES BRIAN.—B.1897; ed. County Schl., Windsor; served in R.G.A. (S.R.), 1915-19; granted rank of capt. on relinquishing commn.; astt. dist. commnr., Gold Coast, 1919; ag. astt. col. sec., 1920; prtv. sec. and A.D.C. 1921 and 1926; ag. astt. col. sec., 1922; ag. dist. commnr., 1922-24; dist. commnr., 1924; astt. col. sec., 1926; col. sec., Gambia, 1931; ag. govr., Gambia, 1931.

PARK, ALEXANDER DALLAS, C.M.G. (1932), F.I.A.N.Z., A.R.A.N.Z.—B. 1882; ed. Waitaki Pub. Schl., Waimate High Schl. and privately; N.Z. pub. wks. dept., 1900-18; agr. dept., 1919; inspr., pub. serv. commnr.'s office, 1920; sec. of marine, 1922; astt. pub. serv. commnr., 1923; astt. sec., treas., 1925; sec., 1930 also financial adviser, 1931; served with N.Z. forces in S. Africa.

PARK, CAPT. EDWARD NIGEL, M.C.—B. 1889; ed. Aldenham Schl.; Somaliland Camel Corps 1917-20; dist. polit. offr., Somaliland, 1920; dist. commnr., Somaliland, Feb., 1922.
PARKER, CECIL JOSEPH, M.C., M.I.C.E.—B. 1888; asst. engrnr., Peru, 1910; asst. engrnr., P.W.D., F.M.S., Jan., 1911; lieut., R.E. (Field Co.), 1915-19; served in France and Italy; ment. in despatches, 1917; M.C., 1918; war and victory medals; ex. engrnr., P.W.D., F.M.S., Jan., 1920; sen. ex. engrnr., P.W.D., F.M.S., Apr., 1927; 1929; ditto, Perak, Nov., 1929; state engrnr., Perak, Jan., 1930.

PARKER, JAMES T.—Cert. teacher, Leeward Is.; dist. postmtr., Bethesda, 1901; schlmr., govt. boys' reformatory schl., 1903; clk. and storekeeper, P.W.D., and clk. to road bd., Antigua, 1906; 1st govt. offr., Virgin Is., 1915; inspr. of weights and measures, Virgin Is., 1917.

PARKER, LANCELOT—B. 1879; clk., cust., Johannesburg, 1902; survr., Cape Town, 1915; served R.F.A. in Great War; cust. investigation offr. for Union in New York, 1926; coll. cust. and shipping mast., Port Elizabeth, 1930.

PARKHILL, ROBERT ARCHADELE.—El. to H. of R., Commonwealth of Australia, 1927; min. for home affrs. and transport, Lyons' ministry, 1932.

PARKINSON, A. C. C., M.A. (1910), C.M.G. (1931), O.B.E.—B. 1884; ed. at Epsom and Oxford; class. demy, Magdalen 1903-7; 1st cls. moda., 1905; 1st cls. lit. hum., 1907; apptd. after compet. exam., 1st cls. clk., acctnt.-gen.'s dept., Admiralty, Feb., 1908; transf. as 2nd cls. clk., C.O., 19th Apr., 1909; sec., man. comte., of imperial bureau of entomology; sec. to comtese, apptd. to investigate relationship between wild animals and trypanosomiasis, 1913-1914; asst. priv. sec. to Mr. Lewis Harcourt, 5th Oct., 1914, to Mr. Bonar Law, 27th May, 1915, to Mr. Walter Long, 11th Dec., 1916; 1st cls. clk., 8th Dec., 1917; on military service from 16th May, 1915 to 26th May, 1919; prin., 1st Apr., 1920; priv. sec. to Lord Milner, 1st Oct., 1920; asst. sec., 1st Oct., 1925; order of the Brilliant Star of Zanzibar, cls. III, 1929; asst. under sec. of state, 15th Aug., 1931.

PARMELEE, JAMES GRANNIS, O.B.E.—B. 1875; inspr., iron and steel bounties, Sydney, Nova Scotia; trade and commerce, Canada, 1902; clk., dept. T. and C., Apr., 1911; on mily. serv., 1914-19 (twice ment. in despatches); head clk., Apr., 1919; ch. clk., Jan., 1921; asst. dep. min. T. and C., Apr., 1923; on sp. duty to U.K., 1928; dep. min., trade and commerce, Nov., 1931.

PARNALL, JOHN.—Solr.; asst. aud., E. Africa Prot., 1915; asst. aud. and in charge, Zanzibar, Nov., 1915; ag. treas., Zanzibar, Sept. 1919 to July, 1920; regar. and offl. assignee, H.B.M. ct., Zanzibar; regar. of patents, designs, and trade marks, Feb., 1920; ag. admstr.-gen. and regar. of docs., Apr. to Oct., 1922; asst. admstr.-gen., Tanganyika Territory, Sept., 1923; ag. admstr.-gen., Oct., 1923 to Jan., 1924; admstr.-gen., pub. trustee, regar. of docs. and land offr., Zanzibar, May, 1924; ag. atty.-gen., June-Dec., 1929.

PARR, HON. SIR CHRISTOPHER JAMES, K.C.M.G. (1925), C.M.G. (1914).—B. 1869; ed. Auckland Gram. Schl. and Auckland Univ. Coll.; barrister-at-law; mem., N.Z. parlmt., 1914-26; min. of educn., 1920-26; min. of health, 1920-23; min. of just., 1923-26; P.M.G. and min. of tele., 1925-26; high commr. for N.Z. in England, 1926-29; M.L.C. and leader of leg. coun., 1931.

PARRY, J. H., B.A. (Cantab.), M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.)—Tempy. coman. in Indian med. serv., Mar., 1915 to Mar., 1919; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Mar., 1919; senr. med. offr., 1928.

PARRY, REGINALD FRANCIS SCARLETT.—Ed., St. John's Schl., Leatherhead, and Lincoln Coll., Oxford; jur. supt., educn. dept., N. Nigeria, Jan., 1920.

PARSONS, CUTHBERT LEO, M.I.R.S.E.—B. 1884; asst. signal and telegr. engrnr., sp. services, F.M.S. Rly., Sept., 1914; dist. signal engrnr., grade II; grade I, Sept., 1923; dist. signal and telegr. engrnr., grade I, Aug., 1928; ditto, F.M.S. Rly., std. to head office, K. Lumpur, June, 1930.

PARSONS, HON. HERBERT ANGAS, LL.B.—Judge of sup. ct., S. Australia, 1921.

PARTIDGE, GEORGE JAMES, B.A. (1915), M.A. (1921), Barrister-at-Law, Middle Temple (1927).—B. 1893; ed. Christ's Hospital and Cambridge; open exhib., (maths.), and Essex County Scholar, Queens' Coll., 1912-14; 2nd cls. maths. tripoe, part I., 1913, B.A. (War), 1915; temp. comm., 1914-18; on active serv. in France and German E. Africa; 1914-15 Star; ment. in desp.; asst. polit. offr., 1st grade, provisional admstr., German E. Africa, Dec., 1918; priv. sec. to ag. admstr., Aug. to Dec., 1919; asst. sec., Oct., 1919; ag. senr. asst. sec., on various occasions, 1921-23; clk. to exec. coun., Sept., 1922 to Sept., 1923; senr.-asst. sec., Aug., 1925; ag. asst. ch. sec., in 1927, 1928 and 1929; asst. ch. sec., Apr., 1930.

PASCHALIS, NEOPTOLEMOS.—B. 1880; barrister-at-law, Middle Temple, 1902; solr.-gen., Cyprus, Mar., 1927; ag. atty.-gen. for various periods, 1927-31.

PASHLEY, EDWARD REYNOLD.—B. 1869; storekeeper, petroleum warehouse, cust., Bahamas, 1893; landing waiter, 1896; senr. clk. of check staff, 1897; cust. offr., excise supervisor, boarding offr., Tobago, 1901; landing waiter, cust., Trinidad, 1902; 5th clk. and paymtr., 1907; 4th clk., 1912; 3rd clk., 1913; comptlr. of cust., regar. of shipping, J.P., Bahamas, 1914; ag. rec-gen. in 1919 and 1920; ch. rev. inspr., Trinidad, Mar., 1921.

PASKIN, JESSE JOHN, B.A., M.C.—B. 1892; ed., King Edwards Schl., Stourbridge and St. John's Coll., Cambridge; 1st cls., maths. tripoe, pt. I., 1913; on mily. serv., Aug., 1914 to Mar., 1919 (Worcestershire Regt., T.F. and Machine Gun Corps); Croix de Guerre, 1918; transf. to T.F. res. with rank of major, Jan., 1920; apptd. under reconstruction scheme, junr. higher divn. clk., min. of transport, Jan., 1920; asst. prin., C.O., 29th Mar., 1921; asst. pvt. sec. to S. of S., 10th Dec., 1928; prin., 4th Sept., 1929.

PASSFIELD, 1ST BARON (CR. 1929) Rt. Hon. SIDNEY JAMES WEBB, P.C., 1924, LL.E. (Lond.), Hon. Doc., Polit. Economy (Munich), etc.—B. 1859; ed. London and abroad; ent. W.O. by open compet., 1878; survr. of taxes, 1879; C.O., cls. I by open compet., 1881; resigned, 1891; sometime hon. lect. on polit. economy at City of London Coll. and Working Men's Coll. and subsequently hon. prof., public admstr., London School of Economics, 1912-27; M.P. (Seaham Divn.), 1922-29; pres. Bd. of Trade, Jan.-Nov., 1924; sec. of state for dom. affrs. and the cols., June, 1929; has served on numerous royal commis. and deptl. comtesse; author of many works on politics and economics.

PASSINGHAM, FRANK SELWOOD.—B. 1883; ed. Goldsmiths' and Morley Colls., Lond.; hon. medallist in typography, City and Guilds of Lond. Inst.; govt. printer, Mauritius, Feb., 1914; also supt., bookbinding works and stat. stores, Apr., 1914; supt. of printing, Jamaica, Mar., 1924; supt., govt. printing office, Cyprus, Oct., 1930.
PATerson, Henry Sibbald.—B. 1890; ed. Winchester Coll. (schol.) and Magdalen Coll., Oxford (exhibr.), B.A., 1913; cadet, F.M.S., Nov., 1913; seconded for war serv., Mar., 1915; active serv. in France and England, 1915-19; ment. in desp.; demob. with rank of major, Aug., 1919; asst. dist. offr., Aug., 1919; seconded as asst. adviser, Trengganu, July, 1920; supernmy. offr., cls. IV., Nov., 1920; dist. offr., Dec., 1923; offr., cls. III., Nov., 1926; asst. advr., Kedah, Apr., 1932.

PATTERSON, Francis Tucker, Dip. oiv. Engng. (Bristol), M. Inst. C.E.—B. 1883; Axminster and Lyme Regis rly., 1901-03; Cape Col. water supply investig., 1903-06; pub. wks. constrn., England, 1907-13; circle engrg., irrign. dept., Union of S. Africa, 1914-19; engrg., Kamanassie irrign. bd., 1919-24; suptg. engrg., irrign. dept., 1924-26; asst. dir., irrign., 1926; ag. dir., irrign., Aug., 1926.

PATTERSON, John Robert.—B. 1892; B.A. (Cantab.); asst. dist. offr., Nigeria, 1915; ag. senr. res., Bornu Prov., Sept., 1923; admtr. offr., cls. I., Aug., 1930; prin. asst. sec., Oct., 1930.

PAUL, Robert James.—B. 1888; sub.-inspr. constab., Trinidad, Sept., 1912; 2nd lieut., Trinidad local forces, Jan., 1913; pay and qr-mr., constab., and senr. supply and transport offr., Trinidad local forces, Nov., 1914, to Oct., 1916, and from Apr. to May, 1917; ag. inspr. of constab. and capt. local forces, Aug., 1915; asst. supt., fire brigade, Nov., 1914, to Nov., 1915, and from Feb. to Mar., 1919; ag. supt., fire brigade, Nov., 1915, to Sep., 1916; J.P. for the colony; ag. chief of police, comdt. local forces, supt. of prison, St. Vincent, Aug., 1919; J.P. for the colony; supt. of pol., Nyamaland, Mar., 1923; ag. contr., pol. and prisons, May, 1925 to Sept., 1926; ag. ch. commr., pol. and ch. inspr., prisons, in 1926, 1929 and 1932.

PAULIN, George.—B. 1886; ed. Canterbury Coll., Univ. of New Zealand, B.Sc., 1906; B.Eng., 1908; pupillage with govt. rlys., New Zealand, with city engrg., Christchurch, and with Selwyn county engrg. and engrg.-in-chief, city of Dunedin drainage; engrg.-surv., P.W.D., N. S. Wales, 1910; dist. engrg., Fiji, 1912; res. engrg., Suva harbr. wka., Fiji, 1916.

PAVLIDES, Stelios.—B. 1892; barrister-at-law, Gray's Inn, 1916; crown coun., Cyprus, Dec., 1927; ag. solr.-gen., for various periods, 1928-31.

PAWAN, James Lenox, M.B., Ch.B., Edin.—B. 1887; ent. med. serv., Trinidad, Jan., 1913; dist. med. offr., Mar., 1916; bacteriologist and pathological regsr., Nov., 1923.

PEACOCK, Hon. Sir Alexander James, K.C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1861; mem. of Austn. Federal Convention, 1897-8; premier of Victoria, 1901-2; later chief sec. and min. for labour, Victoria; min. for educn. and labour, Dec., 1913; premier, treas., and min. of justice, 1914; min. for educn., forests and labour, Nov., 1920-27; speaker, legls. assembly, 1928.

PEACOCK, F.—Asst. supt., pol., Kenya, Jan., 1923.

PEAKE, Harold Gordon, B.Sc. (hons.), Lond., A.C.G.I., A.M. Inst. C.E.—B. 1890; ed. Eltham Coll. and Imp. Coll. of Science and Tech., London; adm. engrg. staff, Rosyth dockyard, 1912; ast. engrg., P.W.D., F.M.S., 1914; mil. wks. service, India, garrison engrg., Peshawar, 1919; engrg., P.W.D., Nigeria, 1924; senr. exec. engrg., 1928; D.P.W., Zanzibar, 1932.

PEARCE, Alexander Hugh Blaxell, L.R.C.P. & S., Edin., L.R.F.P.S., Glas. (1904), L.M., Dublin (1906); D.P.H., Dublin (1918), certif., L.S.T.M., F.R.I., pub. health F.R. Soc. Trop. Med. and Hygiene.—B. 1882; ed. George Watson's Coll., Edin., Univ., and Trin. Coll., Dublin; junr. med. offr., Montserrat, 1907; D.M.O., St. Kitts, 1908; res. med. supt., charitable inst., Antigua and M.O.H. Antigua, 1908; col. surg., Falkland Is., 1912; M.E.C. and M.L.C., J.P.; dormant comsmr. to admtr. govt., Falkland Is.; pres. bd. of health, surg.-capt., F.I. Vols., Aug., 1914; seconded, R.A.M.C., 1916-18; capt., R.A.M.C.; served in France and Far East; C.M.O., Bahamas, 1918; M.L.C. and J.P.; D.M.S. and M.E.C., 1928; ch. med. offr., Fiji, M.L.C. and chmn., cent. bd. of health, Nov., 1930.

PEARCE, Rt. Hon. Sir George Foster, K.C.V.O. (1927), P.C. (1921).—Senator for Western Australia in commonwealth parlmt.; sec. of trades coun. at Perth, 1896; pres., 1899; returned to first Commonwealth Senate, 1901; re-elected, 1906, and elected chmn. of comtees.; min. of defence, C. of A., Apr., 1910 to June, 1913; at Imp. Conf., 1911; min. of defence Sept., 1914; rep. Australia at the Washington Disarmament Conf., 1921; min. for home and territories in Bruce ministry, 1923; vice-pres., exec. coun., June, 1926; min. of defence and govt. leader in senate (Lyons' ministry), 1932.

PEARSON, James Rae, C.I.E.—B. 1871; schol., St. Paul's Schol. and Clare Coll., Cambridge; ent. I. C.S., 1892; held various Indian appts., 1892-1926; ret., I. C.S., Aug., 1926; sec. for Indian affrs., Fiji, 1927.

PEARSON, Joseph, D.Sc. (Liverpool), D.Sc. (Manchester), F.R.S.E., F.L.S.—B. 1881; ed. Liverpool Coll. and Univ. Coll., Liverpool; B.Sc., Victoria Univ. 1st cls. hona., 1902; B.Sc., Liverpool, 1904; M.Sc., 1906; D.Sc., 1908; M.Sc., Manchester, 1920; D.Sc., 1922; dir., Colombo Museum, and marine biologist to Ceylon Govt., 11th Aug., 1910; offr. in charge, pearl fisheries; lecturer in zoology, Univ. Coll., Colombo; editor, "Spolia Zeylanica," "Bulletin of the Ceylon Fisheries," "Memoirs of the Colombo Museum," and author of numerous scientific papers on zoology and oceanography.

PEASE, J. W. K.—Asst. dist. comsmr., E.A.P., Apr., 1914; ag. dist. comsmr., Kenya, 1926.

PEDLER, Frederick Johnson, B.A.—B. 1908; ed. Watford Grammar Schol. and Gonville and Cains Coll., Cambridge; major-schol., 1927-30; Goldsmith's exhibr., 1929; cls. I. divn. 1, hist. tripes, pts. I. and II.; B.A., 1930; Schuldham plate prizewinner; apptd. after compet. exam., asst. prin., C.O., Oct., 1930.

PEDLOW, Joseph Howard, B.A. (N.U.I.).—B. 1889; ed. Queen's Coll., Galway; cadet, S.S. Dee., 1912; Chinese Prot., Penang, Jan., 1913; at Amoy, to study Hokkien, Sep., 1913; Chinese Prot., S'pore, Mar., 1916; treasy. for custodian enemy property and war loan work, May, 1916; collr. of war tax, S'pore, in addition, Mar. to June, 1918; pol. mag., S'pore, Aug., 1919; supernmy. offr., cls. IV., Dec., 1919; asst. prot. of Chinese, S'pore, Sept., 1920; asst. to atty.-gen., S'pore, Dec., 1920; offg. asst. prot. of Chinese, S'pore, June, 1921; pol. mag., Penang, Oct., 1921; mem., rent assessment bd., Penang, munici. comsmr., George Town, Nov., 1921 and Oct., 1924; cls. III., Nov., 1924; prot. Chinese, Penang, Dec., 1924; dep. pres., munic. comsmr., George Town, Penang, (cls. I.B.), in addn., Oct., 1926; registr., sup. ct., in addn.,
Mar., 1927; mem., Mohammedan and Hindu endowments bd., Penang, Oct., 1928; stamp and probate offr., S'pore, Dec., 1930; ag. solr. gen., S.S., Jan., 1931.

PEDRAZA, R.—Asst. dist. commnr., E.A.P., Aug., 1914.

PEEBLES, MAJOR H.W., O.B.E. (1917), D.S.O. (1917).—Joined Canadian M.I., Dec., 1899; 2nd lieut., A.S.C., Sept., 1900; lieut., Nov., 1901; S. African War, Jan., 1900, to May, 1902 (severely wounded, Queen's medal and four clasps, King's medal and two clasps); res. of offrs., June, 1902; A.D.C. to Brig.-Gen. Sir W. H. Manning, K.C.M.G., C.B., Feb., 1903, to June, 1904; Somaliland campaign, Jan., 1903, to June, 1904 (twice men in desp., medal and two clasps); A.D.C. and priv. sec. to Sir B. Sweet-Escott, K.C.M.G., govr. of B. Hond., Oct., 1904; local capt., Nov., 1904; commndg. Belize L.I. volra., Dec., 1904; local major, 1905; ass't res., N. Nigeria, Dec., 1906 to Jan., 1907; ag. priv. sec. to Sir E. B. Sweet-Escott, K.C.M.G., govr. of Leeward Is., Oct., 1907; ass't res., N. Nigeria, Mar., 1908; 3rd class res., N. Nigeria, Jan., 1909; resigned on account of ill-health, June, 1909; elk. and priv. sec. to administrator, Dominica, Mar., 1913; raised and commanded Dom. Defence For., Aug., 1914; served with B.E.F. in France from Oct., 1914; ment. in desp., Jan., 1916, Jan., 1917, and May, 1917; awarded D.S.O., June, 1917; ment. in desp., June, 1919; brevet major, June, 1919; D.A.D.O.S., 3rd Army, B.E.F., June, 1916, to Oct., 1917; D.A.D.O.S., Aldershot Command, May, 1917, to 31st May, 1919; commnr., Virgin Islands, July, 1919; commnr., Montserrat, 25th Feb., 1922; assumed govt., 4th Mar., 1922; admtr., St. Vincent, 1929.

PEEL, SIR WILLIAM, K.C.M.G. (1931), K.B.E. (1928), C.M.G. (1926), B.A., 1896, M.A., 1931—B. 1875; ed. Queens' Coll., Cambridge, 11th wrangler, math. tripos., 1896; cadet, S. Stltmtns., Oct., 1897; passed fin. exam. in Malay, Dec., 1899; dist. offr., Prov. Welleaey, Dec., 1901; ditto, Tampin, F.M.S. June, 1908; seconded as pres., mun. commnrs., Penang, Jan., 1911; offr., Class III., but remained seconded, Jan., 1912; ag. res. councillor, Penang, in addtn., Feb. to Oct., 1917; pres. mun. commnrs., Singapore, July, 1918; offr., Class II., F.M.S., Jan., 1919; joint passage contrlr., Malaya, in addn., Feb., 1919; seconded as food contrlr., Malaya and chmn., shipping cte., May, 1919; chmn., European unemployment comte in addn., Feb., 1921; contr., lab., F.M.S. and S. Stltmtns., Feb., 1922; Br. adviser, Kedah, Oct., 1922; res. coun., Penang, July, 1925; ch. sec., F.M.S., June, 1926; offr. administering govt., S.S. and high commnr., Malay States, May to June, 1927; on sp. duty, London, Mar., 1928; gov. and commdr-in-ch., Hong Kong, Mar., 1930; Kt. of Grace, Order of St. John of Jerusalem; hon. fellow, Queens Coll., Camb., 1932.

PEET, JAMES HERBERT.—B. 1882; elk., audit office, Bahamas, 1904; 4th clk., P.O., 1907; 2nd elk., C.S.O., 1909; 3rd elk., treasy. dept., 1910; ch. elk., P.O., 1913; ch. elk. and ast. examg. offr., customs, 1914; compt'r. of cust., Apr., 1921; ag. recvr.-gen., treas. and temp. mem., exec. coun., on various occasions, 1925-28; ag. postmr., Sept., 1928; has held numerous other ag. appts.; postmr., Sept., 1928.

PELLISSIER, S. H., B.A.—B. 1887; ed. Grey Univ. Coll.; vice prin., Boshof, 1914; prin., Ficksburg, 1917; dir., educn., O.F.S., Dec., 1926.

PEMBERTON, ERNEST WILFRED, J.P.—B. 1874; ent. traffic dept., Cape Govt. rly., 1896; stores dept., 1899; treasy., 1903; audr.-gen. dept., 1906; inland rev. dep., 1910; ag. recr. of rev., Kimberley, 1915; recr. of rev., E. London, 1917; lieut., Cape Peninsula Regt., 1902; res. of offrs., 1913; apptd. to Pretoria Regt. from res. and served in German S.W. Africa campaign, Sept., 1914 to Aug., 1915.

PEMBLETON, EDGAR STANLEY, B.A. (Oxon).—B. 1888; astt. res., N. Nigeria, 1911; res., 1928.

PENNEFATHER, CHARLES EDWARD DE FONBLANQUE.—B. 1882; elk., Gilbert and Ellice Is. Prot., 1908; elk. of peace, 1910; sub-inpr. of constabty., Fiji, 1910; inspr., ditto, 1912; dist. commnr., 1914; ag. dist. commnr., Rewa, and gov. commnr., Nataisir, 1914-15; ag. dist. commnr., Cola East, 1917-18; ag. ch. inspr., Fiji constabty., ag. ch. pol. mag., regnr.-gen., regnr. of sup. ct., regnr. of titles, pub. trustees, regnr. of companies, cust. of enemy property, and cur. of intestate and vacant estates, 1918; dist. commnr., 1922.

PENNINGTON, ARTHUR LAWRENCE, B.A.—B. 1901; ed. Newbury Gram. Schl. and Keble Coll., Oxford; astt. dist. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 4th Sept., 1925.

PENTZ, HERBERT FREDERICK, M.C., M.M.—B. 1886; elk., col. sec.'s office, Cape, 1903; elk., Cape admtrn., 1910; ch. elk., ditto, 1922; pub. serv. inspr., 1930; served in S. African infy. brg. in Great War (overseas); under sec. for pub. wks., Aug., 1931.

PEPPYS, WALTER EVELYN.—B. 1886; ed. at Malvern and Brasenose Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1907; M.A., 1910; cadet, F.M.S., 1908; passed cadet, June, 1911; cls. v., Jan., 1912; dist. offr., Jelebu, Apr., 1912; do., Pasir Puteh, June, 1915; do., offr., Pasir Puteh, Jan., 1918; offr., cls. IV., F.M.S., Jan., 1918; offr., class III., Nov., 1920; fed. sect. for ap. duty, Aug., 1921; offr., cls. II., Nov., 1925; astt. sec. to govt., F.M.S., Nov., 1926; offr. cls. I.B., commnr., lands and mines, Johore, Jan., 1928; under sec. to govt., F.M.S., Mar., 1930; supt., govt. monopolies, S.S., Mar., 1932, and commnr., trade and cust., F.M.S. in addn., Apr., 1932.

PERCY, H. VANE (formerly Baumgartner).—B. 1888; ed., Bedford Grammar Schl.; elk., land settit. dept., O.R.C., Oct., 1902; elk. and typist audit dept., Dec., 1902; elk., audit dept., July, 1904; examr. of accts., audit dept., Jan., 1906; jnr. ast. treas., G. Coast, Jan., 1914; ast. treas., Apr., 1917; ag. ch. ast. treas., Nov., 1919; ag. dep. treas. on several occasions, 1921-28; dep. treas., 1929; ag. treas., July, 1930 and May, 1932.

PERDUE, CECIL GRAHAM.—B. 1891; ed. Trin. Coll., Dublin; police probationer, Hong Kong, Nov., 1912; passed in Chinese, 1915; attached to Punjab police, 1915-16; passed in Urdu, 1916; temp. 2nd lieut., Indian army reserve, 1916-19; ag. astt. supt. police, Hong Kong, 1919; ag. deputy supt. police, 1919 and in 1926 and 1927; J.P., 1920; astt. supt., pol., 1920; astt. census offr., 1921; ag. dir., criminal intelligence, 1924, 1928 and 1929; dir., criminal intelligence, 1930.

PERERA, BENJAMIN FRANKLIN.—B. 1901; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1925; attd., Colombo kach., Jan., 1926; ditto, Anuradhapura kach., Apr., 1926; office astt. Puttalam kach., Oct., 1927; pol. mag., Kalutara, Apr., 1928; office astt., Kandy kach., Nov., 1928; addnl. pol. mag., Columbo, Aug., 1930; addnl. astt. govt. agt., Matara, Aug., 1930.
PERERA, CONRAD BONIFACE PETER, B.Sc. (Lond.)—B. 1903; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Feb., 1927; attd., Badulla kach., Mar., 1927; attd., Anuradhapura kach., Oct., 1927; office asst., Puttalam kach., Apr., 1928; ditto, Ratnapura kach., May, 1930.

PERERA, GEORGE HENRY.—B. 1885; cls. V, Ceylon civ. serv., June, 1930; extra office asst., Ratnapura kach., Nov., 1930.

PERERA, HENRY SAMUEL, M.A. (Lond.), Barrister-at-law, Gray's Inn.—B. 1885; divnl. inspr., schls., Ceylon, Dec., 1922; prin., training coll., Sept., 1932.

PERERA, THEODORE DUNGAN, LL.B. (Lond.)—B. 1895; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., local divn., Aug., 1919; attchd. to Kurunegala kach., Aug., 1919; Jaffna kach., Dec., 1919; pol. mag., Avisawella, July, 1921; ag. pol. mag., W. Prov., Feb., 1923; asst. comnr. of stamps, July, 1923; pol. mag., Pt. Pedro, Oct., 1926; asst. comnr., stamps, Nov., 1926; asst. col. sec., Jan., 1929; asst. to income tax adviser, Sept., 1929; sec. to min. of agr. and lands, July, 1931; asst. comnr., income tax, Feb., 1932.

PEREZ, JOSEPH LEON MATHIEU, LL.B.—B. 1896; ed. St. George's Coll., Weybridge, Surrey; called to bar, Middle Temple, 1917; dep. regisr.-gen., Trinidad, Oct., 1927; ag. regisr. gen., regisr., sup. ct. and marshal in 1928 and 1929; ag. asst. mag., St. George West, ag. solr.-gen., July to Nov., 1929; ag. asst. mag., St. George West, Nov., 1929 to May, 1930; ag. mag., St. George West, June, 1930; do., Victoria, 1932.

PERIES, HERMAN ERIC, B.A. (Cantab), B.Sc. (Lond.)—B. 1906; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., July, 1929; attd. secretariat, July, 1929; attd., Puttalam kach., Jan., 1930; ag. office asst., Kegalla kach., Jan., 1931.

PERKINS, ARTHUR JAMES.—B. 1871; Diplôme de l'école Nationale d'Agriculture de Montpellier 1890; management of farm estates, Tunia, 1890-2; prof. of viticulture and oenology, S. Aust., 1892; sec. for agriculture, 1902-1904; prin. of agric. coll. and prof. of viticulture and oenology, 1904; dir. of agric., 1914.

PERKINS, HUGH WHARTON, C.B.E.—B. 1885; ed. Berkhastmed Sch.; on active serv., Nov., 1914; D.A.R.T., June, 1915; temp. major, July, 1916; temp. lieut.-col. and asst. dir., rly. transport, Nov., 1917; C.B.E. (mil.), June, 1918; demob., Nov., 1919; ag. traf. man., F.M.S. rlya., Feb., 1925; traf. man., F.M.S. rlya., Oct., 1925.

PERKINS, LEICESTER GRANT.—B. 1890; ed. privately and Harrison Coll., Barbados; clk., post office, Barbados, Jan., 1909; 5th clk., audit office, Mar., 1911; 2nd clk., registn. office, Nov., 1913; clk. to master in chancery, May, 1914; 4th clk., savings bank, Jan., 1915; 2nd-lieut., Imperial Army, Mar., 1917, served during war in Egypt and Palestine with 2nd B.W.I. Regt.; 1st-lieut., Oct., 1918; 1st clk., Barbados savings bank, Aug., 1919; 2nd grade super. of cns., Nigeria, Feb., 1920.

PERLEY, RT. HON. SIR GEORGE HALSHEY, P.C. (1931), G.C.M.G. (1933), K.C.M.G. (1916)—B. 1857; ed. Ottawa gram. schl., St. Paul's schl., Concord, N.H., and Harvard Univ.; B.A., 1878; elec. to H. of C. Canada (Argenteuil), 1904; re-elec., 1908 and 1911; chief conservative whip, 1911; mem. of privy coun. for Canada and min. without portfolio in Mr. Borden's cabinet, Oct., 1911; ag. high comnr. in London, 1914; min. of overseas mil. forces, 1916; high comnr., 1917; joint comnr. and plenipotentiary of Canada to sign Peace Treaties, 1919; Canadian del. to League of Nations Assembly, 1921; resigned high comnrship, 1922; re-ele. to H. of C., 1925; sec. of state in Meighen Cabinet, 1926; re-ele., e.g., 1926; min. without portfolio in Bennett adminstr., 1930.

PERRY, SIR ALLAN, KT. BACH. (1904); M.D. (Durham); D.P.H.(Lond.); M.R.C.S. Eng.; L.S.A. Lond.—B.1860; prin. civ. med.offr.and inspr.-gen. of hosp., Ceylon; prin. of Ceylon med. coll., Dec., 1897; major R.A.M.C. (retired); mem. municipal coun., Colombo; late pres. Ceylon branch Br. med. assoc.; del. for Ceylon to Internat. Leprosy Conf., Bergen, 1909; ret., 1916.

PERRY, B. C. G.—B.1886; apptd.after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. serv., and assigned to C.O., 9th Apr., 1906; cler. offr., higher grade, 1st Apr., 1922; regiar., C.O., 7th Sept., 1931.

PERRY, GEORGE McREDIE, M.B., C.M., Glasgow, and St. Mary's hosp., London, F.R.G.S.—Asst. col. surg., Lagos, Oct., 1893; ag. col. surg., Feb. to Mar., 1894; ag. asst. col. sec., May, 1894; med. offr. to expedit. to Idanai mountains; sen. asst. col. surg., Aug., 1895; ag. col. surg., 1896.

PERSSE, CAPT. EDMUND MATURIN, M.C. (1918), F.R.G.S., R. of O., W. Yorks. Regt.—B. 1890; ed. Bedford Mod. Sch.; asst. dist. comnr., Uganda, Oct., 1919; dist. comnr., Apr., 1925.

PETERS, BERNARD R., M.B.E., A.M.I.C.E.—Asst. engrnr., E.A.P., 1914-15; exec. engrnr., Tanganyika, 1919; ag. dep. D.P.W. in 1926 and 1927; D.P.W., Nyassaland, Aug., 1928.

PETRIDES, PHILIP BERTLE.—B. 1881; ed. Dulwich Coll. and Brussels; called to the bar, Middle Temple, 1906; joined Midland Circ. and Birmingham and cent. crim. court sess., 1906; legal adviser and crown prosecutor, Seychelles, Jan., 1916; ex-officio mem. exec. and legis. couns.; ag. chief just., July, 1916 to Mar., 1917, May, 1918 to Oct., 1918, and from Dec., 1918 to Nov., 1919; temp. emplo., C.O., Feb. to Apr., 1920; ch. just., Seychelles, June, 1920; admstd. govt., Mar., 1921 to Sept., 1922; atty.-gen., Nyassaland Prot., 1924; ag. judge, May to Dec., 1925; puisne judge, Nigeria, Sept., 1926; ch. just., Mauritius, May, 1930.

PETRIE, GEORGE MELVIN.—Joined Bech. Prot. pol., June, 1910; treasy. clk., 1922; asct., 1924; ag. finan. sec., master and regisr., deeds, 1922-23 and 1926; ag. finan. sec., mast. and regisr., deeds, 1927; asctnt., Basutoland, Nov., 1927.

PETTMAN, P. A. H.—B. 1896; asct., P.W.D., Zanzibar, 1926.

PHILIPPS, JAMES ERASMUS TRACY, Capt., The Rifle Brigade (Reg. Army R. of O.), M.C. (1916), Ordre de la Couronne of Belgium (1921), M.A., B. Litt., F.R.G.S., F.R.A.I.—B. 1888; ed. Marlborough Coll., Oxford and Durham Univ., ed., Durham Univ.; lieut., 1912; asst. dist. comnr. and addnl. dist. mag., Uganda, 1912, asst. intell. offr., E. Africa Expedy. Force, from Aug., 1914, att. K.A.R.; commanding 2,000 armed levies and scouts from Sept., 1914 (wounded and ment. in despe.); admstd. Kifumbiro (Bukoba) area of occupied territory, Sept., 1914, under martial law; polit. offr. on staff of Major-Gen. J. M. Stewart, C.B., Bukoba Expedy. Forces, June, 1915 (ment. in despe.); capt., Kagera Command Staff, Jan., 1916; ch. polit. offr., Uganda area and N.W. Prove., Tanganyika during oper., Jan., 1916; ch. intell.
offr. (G.S.O.3), on staff of the Lake Command, E.A.E.F., to Tabora, from Aug., 1916; M.C., 1916; in charge of polit. mission in Br. and Belgian areas of conquered territory, Nov., 1916 to Mar., 1917, when invalided, empl. intell. duties, W.O., June to Aug., 1917; attd. Admy. War Staff, intell. div., Aug. to Oct., 1917; employed by F.O. to Abyssinia, 1918; on sp. duty in Sudan, 1918; raised two companies Somalis and Abyssinians for K.A.R. in French and Abyssinian territory, Apr., 1918; ag. dist. commnr., Kigezi, Br. Ruanda, and dist. mag. Kabale, Feb., 1919; made expedit. across Africa from E. to W. via Lake Kivu through Belgian, French and Portuguese territories; Br. commnr. for Russian Red Cross in Russia, 1921; Br. relief commnr. S. Russia, under the L. of N., 1922; mem., Br. comm. for Moslem refugees, Turkey, 1922; "Times" war corres. in Greco-Turkish war, 1922; liaison offr. with French troops and with Greek forces of occupation in Turkey, 1923; mem. Greco-Bulgarian frontier enquiry, 1923; seconded to Sudan govt. as asst. dir. of intell. Khartoum, 1924; commnr., Tembura dist., French frontier, 1925; dist. commnr., Teso (Uganda), 1926; Kigesi, 1928; publications, "Pan-Islam in Africa," "Cape to Cairo developments," "Ruanda" (1919); "The Nabingi" (1919); "A. Kinya-Ruanda Vocabulary" (1920); "Ethiopianism" (1921); "The Turkish Emigration from Thrace" (1922); "The Religion of the Niam-Niam (Zande) People" (1926).

PHILLIPS, HAROLD ERNEST.—B., 1877; clk. to auditor, B. Honduras, Oct., 1892; 5th clk., treas., customs and P.O. depts., June, 1893; 4th clk., Feb., 1894; 3rd clk., treas. and cust. dept., May, 1897; 2nd clk., June, 1898; 2nd clk., C.S.O., Sept., 1900; ch. clk. and clk. of couns., Jan., 1906; priv. sec. to gov. Sir E. Swayne, 1909-10; to gov. Collett, 1911-13; to ag. gov., Walter, 1916; ag. commnr. of currency, Feb., 1911; ag. treas., collr. of cust., 1911-14 and 1917-20; ag. col. sec., 1920; Br. Honduras del. to Canada-W. Indies Conf., Ottawa, June, 1920; asst. col. sec., Apr., 1921; commnr. and judge, Turks and Caicos Is., June, 1923.

PHILLIPS, TREVOR STANLEY, B.A.—Ed., Llandovery Coll., and Jesus Coll., Oxford; instr. sup., educn. dept. N. Nigeria, Sept., 1914; attached, Nigeria Regt., 1917-18; prin., higher coll., Katina, Dec., 1931.

PHILLIPSON, SYDNEY, M.A. (Manchester).—R. 1892; on mily. serv., May, 1915; cadet Ceylon civil serv., Nov., 1919; attchd. to Kandy kach., Dec., 1919; pol. mag., Matara, Sept., 1922; office ast., Kurunegala kach., July, 1924; ast. contr., rev., custodian, enemy property and contr., local clearing office, in addn., Jan., 1925; sec., salaries comm., Nov., 1926; sec., land comm., in addn., July, 1927 to March, 1928; ast. sec., sp. comm., on constitution in addn., Nov., 1927 to Jan., 1928; addnl. ast. com. treas., Nov., 1929 and June, 1930; contr., estab., July, 1931; contr., supplies and finance, July, 1932.

PICKERING, SIR GEORGE HUNTER, Kt. Bach. (1932).—Town mag., E. A.Y., 1910; ag. 2nd puisne judge, 1915; puisne judge, 1917; ag. ch. just., Apr. to Nov., 1927; ch. just., Zanzibar, 1928; ret., 1932.

PICKWORTH, CECIL HENRY.—B. 1890; war serv., in France, 1914-19; attd., experimental dept. of tanks, miny. of munitions, 1917-19; res. engnr., P.W.D., Nigeria, 1921; res. engnr., Singapore municipality, 1924; elec. engnr.-in-ch., P.W.D., Nigeria, 1927.

PIDDUCK, H. R.—Ed. Harper Adams agr. coll., Univ. of Wales; Shropshire Yeomanry, 1914-19; science mast., Dominica Grammar Sch., 1922; headmast., 1923; agr. offr., 1929.

PIENAAR, ANDRIES GUSTAF ERLAND.—Clk. of ct., Lichtenburg, July, 1902; ag. pub. prosecutor, Feb., 1903; pub. prosecutor, June, 1903; ag. asst. res. mag., Feb., 1904; ch. clk. and ag. asst. res. mag., Nov., 1905; addnl. ast. res. mag., Krugersdorp, Sept., 1906; res. mag. and native commnr., Waterberg, Nov., 1910; res. mag., Ermelo, Apr., 1912; senr. mag., Germiston, Mar., 1920; pub. serv. inspr., Sept., 1921; mag., Louis Trichardt dept. of just., Aug., 1924; sec. for int., Dec., 1924; chmn., pub. serv. comm., 2nd Aug., 1926.

PIENAAR, BABEND JACOBUS.—B. 1883; atty.; el., Transvaal prov. coun., 1917; el. S. African parl., 1920; re-el., 1921, 1924, 1929; resigned parl., on appt. as min. plenipotentiary at Rome, 1929.

PIENAAR, MAJOR FILIPPUS FOURIE, D.T.D., O.B.E.—Civ. serv., S. A. Republic; dep. chmn., miner's phthisis bd., Witwatersrand; accredited rep. of Union of S. Africa to League of Nations.

PIERIS, PAULUS EDWARD, Sarasamarina Sri-wardhana, M.A., Trin. Coll., Camb., 1890, L.L.M., D.Litt. (Cantab.)—Barrister-at-law, Inner Temple, 1896; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., 1896; ast. to gov't. agt., Colombo, 1898; pol. mag., Panadura, 1899; dist. judge, Ratnapura, 1899; ast. to gov't. agt., Galle, 1901; ag. dist. judge, Matara, Mar., 1903; office ast. to gov't. agt., Galle, June, 1903; ast. commnr., St. Louis exhibn., Feb., 1904; dist. judge, Kegalle, Mar., 1906; ditto, Kalutara, Mar., 1906; ag. regar. gen., Dec., 1910; ag. dist. judge, Kurunegala, May, 1912; commnr. of requests, Colombo, Nov., 1912; ag. dist. judge, Kandy, Nov., 1913; dist. judge, Galle, June, 1914; ditto, Jaffna, Dec., 1915; ag. dist. judge, Colombo, Mar., 1919; ditto, Kandy, Apr., 1920; dist. judge, Kandy, July, 1921; pub. trustee, Oct., 1928.

PIERS, FRANCIS A.—B. 1883; sub-inspr., Basutoland mounted pol., 1910; inspr., 1923.

PIGGOTT, SIR FRANCIS TAYLOR, KT. BACH. (1905).—Barrister-at-law; employed by F.O. on special service in 1887; legal adv. to prim. min., Japan, Nov., 1887; sec. to att.-gen. Sir C. Russell (afterwards Lord Russell of Killowen) during Behring Sea arbit., 1893-4; proc.-gen., Mauritius, 1894; ag. ch. just., 1895 to 1897; ch. just., Hong Kong, Apr., 1906; ret., 1912; recd. thanks of coun. of govt. for ser. in connection with planters' loans, 1902; author of "Nationality and Nationalization," "Exterritoriality," "Extradition," "Foreign Judgments and Jurisdiction," "Law of Tort," and "Imperial Statutes applicable to the Colonies."

PILBEAM, S. A.—B. 1899; entd. C.O., Jan., 1915; passed ast. clk.'s exam., July, 1916; on military service from 18th July, 1917, to 10th Mar., 1919; assigned to C.O. as ast. clk., Apr.,
1919; cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920; ag cler. offr., higher grade, 10th Oct., 1925.

PILLING, HENRY GUY, C.M.G. (1932).—B. 1886; ed. King's Schol., Ely, and Keble Coll., Oxford; M.A., 1911; cadet, Fiji, 1907; passed cadet, 1910; 2nd grade dist. commnr., 1914; mem., Indian Franchise Comm., 1920; ag. ast. col. sec., 1920; ast. col. sec., Jan., 1921; ag. sec., W. Pacific high commr., Mar., 1924; sec., W. Pacific high commr., 1926; astt. to high commr., W. Pacific, 1929; col. sec., Br. Honduras, Dec., 1929; ag. gov., Apr. to Sept., 1930, Mar. to Apr., 1931 and from Sept., 1931.

PINK, HERBERT JOHN.—(late paymr. lieut. R.N.R.) Ed. Portsmouth Coll., ast. treas., Kenya, and in charge income tax dept., 1920-22; col. treas., St. Helena, 1923; J.P., St. Helena, Feb., 1924; treas. and postmtr., St. Lucia, 1928; O.A.G. and ag. col. sec., Apr. to Sept., 1930.

PINKERTON, WILLIAM JAMES DUNLOP, A.M.I.C.E., Chartered Civil Engrnr.—B. 1890; ast. engrnr., P.W.D., F.M.S., Apr., 1914; exec. engrnr., Ulun Selangor, July, 1923; ar. exec. engrnr., in addn., Jan., 1930; offic. as ar. exec. engrnr., Kinta, in addn., Nov.-Dec., 1930.

PINNEY, CAPT. CHAS. ROBERT, M.C. (1917).—B. 1883; ed. Essendon Grammar Schol.; draughtsman, lands dept., Papua, 1906; on war serv., A.I.F., 1914-20; wounded; transf'd. R. of O., C.M.F., 1920; ch. draughtsman, Papua, 1920; staff survr. in addn., 1924; ag. commr., lands, etc., 1927; commr., lands, dir. mines, dir. agr., dep. commr., land bd., mem. exec. and leg. couns., July, 1930; admstr., Norfolk Is., July, 1932.

PIRIE, D.A.—B. 1886; clk. Burgher camps, Transvaal, 1902; treasry., 1903; prin. clk. treasry., Union of S. Africa, 1920; sec. mily. pensions bd., treasry., 1920; ch. clk., grade II, 1928; ch. clk., grade I, 1932.

PIROW, HANS, D.Sc., M.Inst.M.M., D.I.C., vice-pres., Geol. Soc. of S.A.; mem., coun., Chem. Met. and Min. Soc., and S.A. Assoo. for the Adv. of Science.—B. 1892; ed. S. Africa and on continent; grad., S.A. and London; various offl. capacities on Witwatersrand gold mines, 1911-1919; govt. research schol., 1919-20; ast. inspr., mines, 1920; dominion sci. schol., London, 1924; G.M.E., Dec., 1926; is also chmn., mining leases bd. and elec. control bd., assessor mem., research grant bd. and statistical coun.; ag. sec., mines and industries, 1927.

PIROW, OSWALD.—B. 1890; ed. South Africa, Germany and England; admitted barrister, 1915; K.C., 1925; ent. parl., of the Union of S. Africa, 1926; min. of justice, June, 1929.

PITCAIRN, ANDREW.—B. 1894; ed. Edinburgh Coll. of Agr.; on war serv., 1915-19 (France, Mesopotamia and Palestine); lieut., R.F.A.; ment. in desps.; dist. agrl. offr., Tanganyika Territory, June, 1921; astt. dir., agr., Cyprus, Mar., 1929; ag. dir., agr., June-Nov., 1930; ag. dir., animal hu-bandry, June to Sept., 1930, and June-Sept., 1932.

PITMAN, CHARLES ROBERT SENHOUSE, D.S.O. (1917), M.C. (1916).—B. 1890; ed. Royal Naval Schol., Blundell's and R.M.C., Sandhurst; att'd. R. Warwickshire Regt.; 27th Punjabis; capt., 1915; war serv., Egypt, 1914-15; France, 1915; Mesopotamia, 1916-18 (wounded, desps. twice, M.C., D.S.O.); Palestine, 1918-21; gen. staff, 1919-21; game warden, Uganda, 1925.

PITOT, LÉON EMILE, O.B.E. (1930).—B. 1866; govt. survr. and supt. of pub. wks., Seychelles, 14th Apr., 1889; govt. engnr. and architect, Mauritius, Apr., 1891; gen. man. of rwy. and engineer, Mauritius, 14th Sept., 1896; chmn., bd. of commrs., Curepipe.

PITT, WALTER JAMES, B.A.—B. 1875; ed. Downing Coll., Cambridge (modern and medieval language tripos); ent. Middle Temple, Jan., 1919; passed Bar final exam., Dec., 1920; headmst., Cape Coast Govt. Schol., 1910; inspr. of schls., 1912; prov. inspr. of schls., 1914; astt. to polit. serv., Gold Coast, Aug., 1914; astt. dist. commr., July, 1917; dist. commr., Jan., 1921; ag. prov. commr., W. Prov., Ashanti, Feb.-Nov., 1920.

PITTMAN, WILLIAM.—B. 1878; ed. S. African Coll. and Wadham Coll., Oxon; B.A. (Univ. S.A.), M.A. (Oxon); called to bar, Middle Temple, 1903; admitted to Cape (1904) and Transvaal (1905) bars; dean of faculty of law, Univ. S.A., 1918-25; K.C., 1924; judge, sup. ct., S. Africa eastern dist., local divn., 1925; mem., delimitation comm., 19th July, 1927.

PLANT, GEORGE FREDERIC, C.B.E. (1927).—B. 1877; ed. Manchester Gram. Schol. and Brasenose Coll. (scholar, 1896); 1st cl. class. mods., 1898; B.A., 1900; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., 1901; off. astt., Kurunegala, 1902; off. astt., Galie, 1904; pol. mag., Avissawella, 1905; dist. judge, Ratnapura, Apr., 1906; ditto, Matare, Dec., 1906; astt. govt. agt., Kalutara, May, 1909; temporarily employed in C.O. London, May, 1915, to Dec., 1918; sec., overseas settlement comm., Jan., 1919; permanently transferred to Home civ. serv. Sept., 1919; mem., overseas settlement delegtn. to Canada, 1924.

PLATTS, SHELLEY ARDEN.—B. 1899; ed. Bedford Schol.; passed army entrance exam.; "King's India cadetship," 1917; gazetted 2/9th Gurka Rifles; 3rd Afghan War, 1919; astt. 2/11th Gurka Rifles and 4/70th Burma Rifles, Burma, 1921; cadet, adm'tive. service, Tanganyika Territory, May, 1926; astt. dist. offr., July, 1928.

PLOWMAN, CLIFFORD HENRY FITZHERBERT, O.B.E. (1928).—B. 1889; ed. at King's Schol., Ely and Trin. Coll., Camb.; B.A. (class. tripos); astt. dist. commr., E. Africa Prot., Mar., 1912; pol. offr., Turkana Expdn., 1915 (A.G.S. Med. with clasps); ag. offr. in charge, Northern Frontier Dist., 1919-20; seconded to F.O. as H.B.M. Vice-Consul, Harar, Abyssinia, 1920; H.B.M. Consul on transfer Harar Consulate to C.O., 1922; transf'd., Somaliland, 1922; H.B.M. chargé d'affaires, Addis Ababa, Dec., 1925 to Jan., 1926; 2nd cls., Star of Ethiopia; mem., mission to Abyssinia for coronation of Emperor, 1930; has passed E. Africa law exam. and in Swahili, Boran Galla and Amharic languages.

PLYMOUTH, 2nd Earl of (cr. 1905) and 15th Baron Windsor (cr. 1529) IVOE MILES WINDSOR-CULVER.—B. 1889; ed. Eton and Trinity Coll., Cambridge; D.L., Worcestershire; lord-lieut., Glamorganshire, 1923; capt., hon. corps of gentlemen-at-arms, 1925; M.P., Ludlow divn., Shropshire, 1922-23; parl. under-sec. of state for Dominion affrs., Jan., 1929; kt. of grace of St. John of Jerusalem; parl. sec., min. of transport, Sept., 1931; parl. sec., min. of transport, Sept., 30th Sept., 1932.

POLE-EVANS, ILIETTO BULLER, C.M.G. (1921), M.A. (Cantab.), D.Sc. (Wales), F.L.S.—B. 1879; ed. Cowbridge Gram. Schol. and Univs. of Wales and Cambridge; mycologist, Transvaal, 1906; rep. Transvaal govt. at 4th Internat. Botanical
Congress, Brussels, 1910; ch., divn. of mycology and plant pathology, 1911; ch., divn. of botany and plant pathology, 1912; sp. mission to P.E. Africa, coconut palm disease, 1913; dir., botanical survey of S. Africa, 1918; pres., S. African Assn. for Advancement of Science, 1920; ch., divn. of botany, horticulture and entomology, 1927; ch., divn. of plant industry, 1929; author of many scientific papers.

POLLARD, ARNOLD.—B. 1893; ed. Heles Schl., Exeter; active serv., R.N.A.S. and R.N.R., 1915-19; col. audit dept., Feb., 1920; asst. audr., Tanganyika Territory, Apr., 1920; asst. audr., Kenya, May, 1924; ag. senr. asst. audr. on several occasions in Tanganyika and Kenya; audr., Windward Is., Jan., 1926; senr. asst. audr., Uganda, Jan., 1929; ag. audr., Apr., 1929; audr., Trinidad, June, 1931.

POOLEY, CHARLES EDWARD.—B. 1903; apptd. after compet. exam., cler. offr., C.O., 22nd Oct., 1920.

POPE, GEORGE WILLIAM, L.L.M.R.C.P., and S.I. (Ireland), D.P.H., R.C.P. and S.I.—Med. offr., Kenya, 1920; 2nd health offr., port med. dept., Hong Kong; ag. asst. bacteriologist, 1924; asst. med. offr. of health, 1925; med. offr. of health, 1926.

POPE, LAWRENCE HENRY.—B. 1896; ed. Uppingham; served European War, 1915-19 (France and N. Russia); asst. P.S. to govrr., S. Australia, Sir W. E. E. A. Weigall, K.C.M.G., 1920; P.S. to govrr., Tasmania, Sir W. L. Allardyce, G.C.M.G., 1921; col. audit dept., 1923; asst. audr., Fiji, 1923; ag. audr., 1924-28; asst. audr., Tanganyika Territory, 1928.

POPE, STEAD.—Br. post office, Feb., 1903; dist. survr., post and tels., Gold Coast, Dec., 1913; on active serv., Togoland Field Force, Aug., 1914; and later in charge posts and tels., Togoland to May, 1915; Imp. army serv., Sept., 1915-19; lieut., R.E. and R.A.F.; dist. survr., Gold Coast, June, 1919; div. survr., Jan., 1927; P.M.G., Nyasaland, Mar., 1930.

POPHAM, HENRY BRADSHAW, M.B.E. (1918).—B. 1881; ed. Tonbridge Schl.; comrn., 13th Light Infy., 1900; served, S. African War (2 med.); seconded, G. Coast regt., 1906; priv. sec. and A.D.C. to ag. govrr., G. Coast, Mar. to Aug., 1909; col. sec.'s office, Jan., 1910; priv. sec. to ag. govrr., Feb. to June, 1911; ag. ch. asst. col. sec. and clk. of couns., July to Aug., 1913; ag. senr. asst. col. sec., Oct., 1913; dist. comrn., Jan., 1914; seconded to Togoland polit. adminstr., Nov., 1914; senr. asst. col. sec. and clk. of couns., Jan., 1920; ag. ch. asst. col. sec., Sept., 1920 to Feb., 1921; dep. prov. comrn. and ag. comrn., W.Prov., Feb., 1921; prov. comrn., Apr., 1922; retd. (invalided) May, 1923; comrn., Cyprus, Oct., 1925.

POPPLEWELL, GEOFFREY DOUGLAS, B.A. (Oxon).—B. 1904; cadet, provincial adminstr., Tanganyika Territory, April., 1927; asst. dist. offr. May, 1929.

POSTMUS, JOHANNES.—B. 1877; ed. in S. Africa and at Sneek, Holland; gen. man., Netherlands Bank of S.A., 1920-26; dep. govrr., S. African Reserve Bank, 1927-31; govrr., S. African Reserve Bank, Jan., 1932.

POTTER, JOHN WAGNER.—B. 1873; ed. at Uppingham Schl. (class. schol.); called to bar, Middle Temple, 1910; ent. Crown Agents office, Oct., 1896; asst. registr., inscribed stock, Mar., 1905; asst. head, gen. stores dept., Jan., 1913; ditto, gen. dept., Jan., 1920; ditto, pay dept., Jan., 1924; dep. head, pay dept., Feb., 1930.

POTTINGER, JOSEPH HECTOR, M.B., Ch.B., D.P.H., D.T.M. & H. (Lpool).—B. 1896; on war serv., 1915-18; med. offr., health, W. African med. staff, Gold Coast, 1928; asst. govt. med. offr. of health, Br. Guiana, 1932.

POTTS, HUGH CUTHBERT MILLER.—B. 1907; ed. Durham Schl. and Lincoln Coll., Oxford; B.A. Law.; cadet, Tanganyika Territory, July, 1930.

POTTS, JOHN WILFRED.—Served in Bechuanaland Prot. pol., 1912-15; clk., 1915; ag. asst. res. mag., 1920; ag. res. mag., 1920 and 1922-23; passed civ. ser. lower law exam., 1919; passed 2nd grade Seowana exam., 1922; sub. inspr., Beoh. Prot. pol., 1924; inspr., Mar., 1927; res. mag., Apr., 1929.

POUGNET, EDOUARD DESBARRIERES, A.C.G.I., A.M.I.C.E.—Pub. wks. dept., Mauritius, Jan., 1888; asst. water authority, Moh., 1898; inspr. of water wks., July, 1903; govt. survr., Moh., 1911; aspt. of pub. wks. and survr. of roads, St. Kitts, Apr., 1914; in service of French govt., in France during the war.

POULIER, REGINALD SYDNEY VERNON.—B. 1894; B.A., Lond.; cadet, Ceylon civ serv., local divn., Aug., 1919; att. Galle kach., Aug., 1919; pol. mag., Matale, Feb., 1922; addnl. dist. judge, Mannar and Mullaitivu, Oct., 1924; addnl. asst. govt. agt., Colombo, Dec., 1925; commr. requests, Kandy, Oct., 1927; asst. govt. agt., Mullaitivu, Nov., 1928; asst. govt. agt., Colombo, Oct., 1931.

POUSSETTE, HENRY RIVINGTON.—B. 1872; ed. Sarnia Pub. Sch., Upper Can. Coll., Royal Mily, Coll., Kingston, and Sch. of Prac. Science, Toronto; capt., S. African Constab., 1901, and thereafter in same corps throughout S. African serv.; dist. comdr., and pub. pros., S. Africa; ent. serv. dept. of trade and commerce, Can., as trade comrn., Durban, S. Africa, 1909; trade comrn., Buenos Aires, 1910; enlisted for active serv.; returned, Can., 1919; inspr., trade comrn. serv.; sp. trade comrn., India, 1919; dir., comm. intelligence serv., Ottawa, 1921; trade comrn., Trinidad, 1924.

POWERS, HON. SIR CHARLES, K.C.M.G. (1929).—Justice of the high ct. of Australia, 1913; ret.

POYNTON, ARTHUR HILTON.—B. 1905; schol. of Marlborough Coll. (1918-23) and Brasenose Coll., Oxford (1923-7); 1st cls. honos., moda., 1925; 2nd cls. honos., lit. hum., 1927; M.A., 1933; apptd. asst. prin., dept. of scientific and industrial research after compet. exam., 31st Oct., 1927; transf. to C.O., 1st Oct., 1929; joint sec. Col. Development Advisory Comtee., 1st Apr. to 30th Sept., 1930; sec., do., 1st April, 1932; pte. sec. to partly. under sec. for cols. (Sir R. Hamilton), 18th April, 1932 and to (Lord Plymouth), 30th Sept. 1932.

POYSER, KENNETH ELLISTON, D.S.O., K.C. (Barbados).—B. 1882; ed. Shrewsbury and Merton Coll., Oxford; called to bar, Inner Temple, 1906; served, European War, 1914-20; Yorks. L.I., and Loyal N. Lanc. Regt. (deeps. thrice, D.S.O., 1917); puisne judge, Leeward Islands, Sept., 1920; atty.-gen., Barbados, June, 1925; atty.-gen., Uganda, 1928.

PRAIN, LT.-COL. SIR DAVID, KT. BACH. (1912); C.M.G. (1912); C.I.E. (1906); M.A., M.B., LL.D., F.R.S.E., F.L.S., F.R.S.—B. 1867; ed. Aberdeen gram.schl. and Univs. of Aberdeen and Edinburgh; demonstrator of anatomy, coll. of surgeons, Edin., 1882-3, and univ. of Aberdeen, 1883-1884; entd. Indian med. serv., 1884; curator, Calcutta herbarium, 1887-1898;
prof. of botany, med. coll., Calcutta, 1895-1905; director, botanical survey of India, and supt. of royal botanic garden, Calcutta, 1898-1905; trustee of the Indian Museum, 1898-1904; sec. bd. of scientific advice for India, 1903-1904; mem. of coun. of various scientific societies; director of royal botanic gardens, Kew, 1905; ret., 1922.

PRANKERD, HORACE ARTHUR, B.A.(Cantab.).—B. 1883; ed. at Ipswich and Queen's Coll., Cambridge (scholar, 2nd class. tripes), B.A., 1905; baccalaureat (B.L. 1st part) Lyons Univ., France, 1908; asst. sec., N. Nigeria, Oct., 1910; asst. res., 1911; ag. supt., schla., July, 1912 to Apr., 1913; called to bar, Gray's Inn, Apr., 1921; promoted cls. I., grade I., adm. serv., Feb., 1928.

PRASAD, MUBARI, U.B.—B. 1888; Cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1912; attached to Galle Kachcheri, Jan., 1913; addtl. office asst. to govt. agt., N.C. Prov., Aug., 1914; addtl. dist. judge, Anuradhapura, Aug., 1915; office asst. to govt. agt., N.C. Prov., Dec., 1915; pol. mag., Chilaw, Apr., 1917; ditto, Panadure, Apl., 1919; office asst. to govt. agt., N. Prov., Mar., 1920; dist. judge, Anuradhapura, May, 1921; pol. mag., Kalutara, May, 1922; ditto, Gampola, Mar., 1923; dist. judge, Tangalla, Oct., 1924; dep. fiscal, Colombo, Feb., 1926; dist. judge, Matara, June, 1927; comsnr., stamps, July, 1932.

PRENDERGAST, HON. JAMES EMILE PIERRE.—Ed. at Seminary of Quebec, and Laval Univ., Quebec; B.A., 1878; LL.B., 1881; returned for La Verendrye, Manitoba, Aug., 1885; again Dec., 1886; on formation of cabinet by Hon. Thomas Greenway, Jan., 1888, was given portfolio of prov. sec.; re-elected in said constituency; elected for Woodlands, 1888; judge of sup. ct., N.W.T., 1902; ditto, Saskatchewan, 1907; puisne judge, court of King's Bench of Manitoba, 1910; oh. just., Dec., 1929.

PRESCOTT, ARTHUR STANLEY.—Apptd. after compet. exam., supplementary clk., supreme ct., Gibraltar, 1895; 3rd cls. clk., 1899; asst. regar. and deputy clk. of arraigna, 1911.

PRETORIUS, Jan Lodewyk.—B. 1878; ed. at Grey Coll., Bloemfontein; joined O.F.S. repub. civ. serv., Mar., 1887; asst. mag., Edenburg, 1902; Vrede, 1904; Lindley, 1908; dist. asst. mag., Dewetsdorp, Feb., 1910 to Oct., 1913; Reitz, Nov., 1913; mag., Reitz, 1918; Hoopstad, Feb., 1919; Boshof, Oct., 1919; Frankfort, Oct., 1923; Senekal, June, 1929; Vereeniging, Feb., 1930.

PRETTY, ERIC ERNEST FALK.—B. 1891; ed. Harrow, and Demy of Magdalen Coll., Oxford; cadet, S.S., Nov., 1914; passed cadet, June, 1917; ag. collr. of land revenue, Johore Bahru, Sept., 1917; offr., cls. V., S.S., Dec., 1917; 2nd lieut. and asst. adlt., J.V.R., May, 1918; supermy. offr., cls. IV., Nov., 1921; Br. rea., Brunei, Mar., 1923; offr., Cls. III., Nov., 1926; dist. offr., Krian, June, 1928; ag. sec., high comsnr., July, 1931; offr., cls. II., Nov., 1931.

PRICE, CHARLES ROY.—B. 1893; ed. Wellington Schl., Somerset and University Coll., London; B.A. (war), 1919; unattached list, Territorial Force, Jan. to Aug., 1915; Royal Garrison Arty., Sept., 1915 to Dec., 1918; served in France, June, 1916 to Sept., 1918; apptd. under reconstruction scheme, asst. prin., C.O., 1st Mar., 1921; pvt. sec. to perm. under sec. for dom. affrs., 6th July, 1927 (ag. from 6th June, 1927); temp. ag. prin., D.O., 22nd July, 1927; pvt. sec. to parly. under sec. for dom. affrs., Jan., 1928; asst. sec., Imp. wireless and cable confce., Jan.-July, 1928; ag. prin., D.O., 15th Sept., 1928; U.K. delegn. to L. of N. assembly, 1928 and 1932; U.K. delegn. to London naval confce., 1930; attd. to sec., Imp. confce., 1930; U.K. delegn., disarmament confce., Geneva, Feb., Dec., 1932.

PRICE, HERBERT HENRY.—2nd clk. to asst. comsnr., Northern Div., Bech. Prot., 1910; 2nd clk., res. comsnr.'s office, 1st May, 1912; passed Cape civ. ser. lower law exam., 1910; ag. asst. res. mag., 1911-12; regar. of brands, 1913; ch. clk. and regar., 1921; passed 3rd grade Seawana exam., 1927.

PRICE, STANLEY LEWIS, B.A.—B. 1891; ed. Lampeter Coll., and Jesus Coll., Oxford; jnr. supt., educn. dept., N. Nigeria, Sept., 1914; attached, Nigeria Regt., 1917-18.

PRICK-JONES, CAPT. WILLIAM.—Served during Great War in France; awarded M.C., 1917; asst. dist. comsnr., Gold Coast, Aug., 1919; dist. comsnr., Apr., 1924; called to bar, Gray's Inn, Nov., 1926; pol. mag., 1928.

PRICHARD, HERBERT WILLIAM, K.C. (1923)—B. 1873; ed. at Keble Coll., Oxford (open class. scholar, 1892); called to the bar, Gray's Inn, Jan., 1902; practised in London, 1902-1910; stip. mag., Trinidad, Aug., 1910; puisne judge, Mauritius, Feb., 1915; 1st puisne judge, Oct., 1916; ag. procureur and advoc.-gen., Oct., 1916 to July, 1917; chrmn., sugar sales comte., Sept., 1918 to Aug., 1919; ag. col. sec., Sept. to Dec., 1920 and Feb. to Apr., 1921; ag. procureur and advoc.-gen., April, 1921; confirmed in appt., Jan., 1922; ag. col. sec. from Aug., 1924 to Feb., 1926; puisne judge, S. Stiltsms., June, 1927.

PRING, HARRY.—B. 1883; ed. Watford Schl. and King's Coll., London; imp. serv., 1898-1903; col. sec.'s office, Capetown, 1903; dept. of interior, Pretoria, 1910; ch. clk., 1922; under sec., 1927; pub. serv. comsnr., 1931.

PRIOR, A. C. VINCENT.—B. 1881; ed. King's Coll., Cambridge; M.A., LL.B.; called to the bar, Inner Temple, 1906; atty.-gen., St. Vincent, Jan., 1915; ag. oh. just., Jan. to June, 1915; atty.-gen., Leeward Is., 1918; solr.-gen., Sierra Leone, Sept., 1920; ag. atty.-gen. on several occasions; solr.-gen., Gold Coast, 1925; ag. atty.-gen., May to Nov., 1926; atty.-gen., Sierra Leone, 1927; ag. ch. just., June to July, 1928 and June to Oct., 1929; atty.-gen., Nigeria, Oct., 1929.

PRITCHETT, CECIL JOHN SUCKLING, B.A. (Oxon.)—B. 1888; cadet, Ceylon civil serv., Dec., 1912; attached to Jaffna Kachcheri, Jan., 1913; ag. pol. mag., Trincomalee, July, 1913; ag. asst. settlmt. offr., Nov., 1913; office asst. to govt. agt., N. Prov., Nov., 1914; asst. collr. of customs and landing survr., Jaffna, Nov., 1914; ag. asst. govt. agt., Mannar, Dec., 1915; office asst. to govt. agt., N. Prov., Feb., 1916; pol. mag., Avissawella, Oct., 1916; ditto, Panadure, Dec., 1917; ditto, Chilaw, Apl., 1918; ag. ditto, Galic, Sept., 1919; asst. land stlitmt. offr., Nov., 1921; dist. judge, Anuradhapura, Feb., 1922; dep. rubber contr., Nov., 1924; asst. govt. agt., Batticaloa, Dec., 1926; dist. judge, Ratnapura, Nov., 1928; dist. judge, Jan., 1932.

PROBYN, SIR LESLIE, K.C.M.G. (1909); C.M.G. (1903).—Ed. at Charterhouse, and in France and Germany, called to the bar, Mid. Tem., 1884; joint author of "The Jurisdiction and Practice of the Mayor's Court," and other law books; atty.-gen., Br. Honduras, 1893; atty.-gen. of Grenada, May, 1896; also ag. col. sec. in 1897-8; ag. admstr. on several occasions; gov. secretary, S. Nigeria, Apr., 1901; gov., Sierra
Leone, July, 1904; gov., Barbados, Nov., 1910; gov., Jamaica, May, 1918; ret., 1924.

PROBSTING, HON. W. B., C.M.G. (1918).—M.L.C., Tasmania; atty.-gen. and min. for rly., Apr., 1916; pres., leg. coun., 1926.

PROUT, SIR WILLIAM THOMAS, K.C.M.G. (1928), KT. BACH. (1924), C.M.G. (1905), O.B.E., M.B., C.M. (Edin.)—Asst. poor law med. offr., Mauritius, 1885; surg. supt., immigrant ship "Dundee," 1887; asst. col. surg., Gold Coast, 1888; dist. comsnr., Gold Coast, 1890; col. surg., Gambia, 1893; ag. chief mag., Gambia, 1893; med. offr. in charge of base hosp. during campaign against Foday Sila; col. surg., S. Leone, 1896; title altered to prin. med. offr., 1901; retired, 1906; fellow of roy. med. soc., Edin., and correspndg. mem. of the epidemiological soc. of Lond.; lect., schl. of trop. med., Univ. of Liverpool; med. adviser to C.O.; mem. of advisory, med. and sanitary comttee. for Tropical Africa, C.O.; senr. med. adviser to C.O., 1924; author of article "Yaws" in "Diseases of Warm Climates" (Davidson); Jnl. Voloulois (Archives de Parasitologie, May, 1901); "Filariasis in S. Leone" (Brit. Med. Journal, 1902); and other papers.

PRYER, JOHN HAWKES.—B. 1894; ed. Bedford Harpur Trust; mech. transport, B.E.F., France, 1918-19; cadet pilot, R.A.F.; asst. storekeeper, Gold Coast rly., Sept., 1920; asst. ch., do., Aug., 1929; ch., do., Mar., 1932.

PUCRIDGE, GEOFFREY MARTIN.—B. 1895; ed. Exeter Schl.; 2nd lieut., Devon Regt., T.F., Dec., 1913; capt., Dec., 1914; served in France with 5th West Yorks regt.; seconded to Royal Flying Corps, July, 1917; seconded to Inter Allied Aeronautical Comn. of Control, Germany, 1920; re-signed comn., Sept., 1921; asst. dist. comsnr., Gold Coast, 1921; dist. comsnr., 1925; asst. col. sec., 1928.

PUDSEY, FAWCOTT, —B. 1882; Assoo. M.I.M.E.; Assoo. M.I.C.E.; ed. Hymer's Coll., Hull, and Repton Schl.; apprentice with Messrs. Rose, Downs and Thompson, Ltd., Hull, 1900-1905; engineering asst., dock engr.'s staff, N.E. Rly., 1905-1911; engaged on survey work, Catalonia, Spain, for the Pearson Engineering Corporation, New York, 1911; in charge of opening of the Hassle quarry and crushing plant of the British Portland Cement Manufacturers, Ltd., 1912-1914; asst. D.P.W., B. Guiana, 1914; ag. D.P.W., Feb., 1916; D.P.W., Palestine, 1927.

PUGH, S. R., M.B.E. (1928).—B. 1877; apptd., after compet. exam., elk. of the 2nd div. of the civil ser., and assigned to the C.O., Aug., 1897; promoted, with gratuity, Aug., 1904; conf. elk., Dec., 1907; minor staff clerk, 1911; staff elk., 1st grade, 1st Mar., 1916; staff offr., 1st Apr., 1922; on service in Sierra Leone, Oct., 1926 to Feb., 1927; sec., Discovery comttee., Jan.-June, 1928.

PURCELL, SIR GILBERT KENHOLM TREFFRY, KT. BACH. (1916).—Ed. Exeter Coll., Oxford; B.A. 1888; M.A. 1893; called to bar, Linc.'s Inn, Nov., 1890; mem. of western circ., also practised at cent. crim. ct.; apptd. asst. to atty.-gen. Leeward Islds. (St. Kitts), Mar., 1898; official mem. of exec. and legis. couns. of the presidency of St. Christopher and Nevis; ag. atty.-gen. Leewards, Aug.-Oct., 1900; apptd. ag. 1st puisne judge, June, 1901; puisne judge, G. Coast, 11th June, 1901; chief justice, Sierra Leone, 1911.

PURCELL, HUBERT KENNEDY.—B. 1884; ent. Crown Agents office, Oct., 1901; asst. cashier, July, 1914; head of pay dept., Dec., 1920; dep. head of pay and checking dept., Nov., 1921; dep. head, pay dept., 1924; dep. head, gen. dept. and dep. ch. olk., 1930.

PURILL, FREDERICK JOHN.—B. 1891; conf. shorthand writer, B. of T., Aug., 1909; conf. elk. to gen. man., lab. exchange dept., B. of T., Oct., 1909; conf. shorthand writer to S. of S., H.O., Jan., 1911; cler. offr., 21st Jan., 1925; accompanied the Rt. Hon. L. S. Amery, M.P. (S. of S. for Dominion Affairs) on his tour of the Dominions visiting S. Africa, S. Rhodesia, Australia, New Zealand, Fiji and Canada, Aug., 1927-Feb., 1928; transferred to C.O., June, 1928; accompanied Br. economic mission to Australia as offr. shorthand writer, Feb., 1929.

PUTTICK, LEONARD JAMES.—B. 1885; ed. at High Schl. and Huguenot Coll., Wellington and S. African Coll., Cape Town; served Anglo-Boer war, 1900-01; draughtsman, Swaziland, 1910; elk. of lands, 1916; ch. elk., 1919; ag. regisr. and mast., sp. ct. and sheriff, 1919; sec., Swaziland-Portuguese bdry. comn., 1922; sec., undeveloped minerals comn., 1927; ag. dept. asst. comn., 1925 and 1930; beacon inspr., 1927; ag. govt. sec. in 1927 and 1928; asst. govt. sec., 1928; regisr. and mast., sp. ct., sheriff, regist., births, marriages and deaths and comn., protocols, 1932.

QUIGLEY, EUGENE PATRICK, M.C.—B. 1889; served six years R.I.C.; joined army, 1914; 2nd lieut., R. Dublin Fusiliers, 1915; served in France, Egypt and Palestine; organised pol., C.I.D., Palestine, 1919; D.C.P., grade I, 1921; dist. asupt., pol., Apr., 1926; dep. comdt., C.I.D., 1930.

RAE, SIR JAMES STANLEY, KT. BACH. (1933)—B. 1881; articled and conf. elk. to Sir W. R. Davies, Kt., when atty.-gen., Bahamas; called to the bar, Bahamas, Apr., 1904; called to the bar, Middle Temple, Jan., 1919; ag. coroner for the Is. of New Providence from 1904, confirmed in 1911; J.P., 1910; ag. atty.-gen., Jan., 1910; ag. stip. and circ. mag., 1910-11, and on other occasions; dist. comsnr., Belize, B. Honduras, 1914; off. recr. in bankruptcy, off. admstr. and J.P. for the col., 1914; regisr.-gen., Nov., 1915, in conjunction with duties as dist. comsnr.; dir. of P.O.G. fund, 1916; custodian of enemy property, Sept., 1916; press censor during war; pvt., B. Hond. Territorial Force; addl. to staff as mily. censor; atty.-gen., St. Vincent, Apl., 1919; cross of Chevalier of the Order of the Crown, Belgium, for relief services during war, May, 1919; ag. ch. just., St. Vincent, June to Oct., 1919; atty.-gen., St. Lucia, Sept., 1920; ag. ch. just., June, 1921 to Feb., 1922 and from Sept., 1922 to June, 1923; ch. just., St. Vincent, June, 1923; ag. admstr., June, 1926 to Feb., 1927; ch. just., Grenada, 1927; revised and consolidated laws, 1926; ch. just., Leeward Is., Apr., 1931.

RAE, NORMAN.—B. 1892; entd. Crown Agent's office, May, 1911; asst. head of dept., May, 1919; dep. head, stores dept., Oct., 1932.

RAEBURN, COLIN, D.Sc., F.G.S.—B. 1894; ed. Hamilton Acad. and Glasgow Univ.; lient. Cameron Highlanders, 1915-19; Salonika, 1915-18; geologist, Scottish Spitzbergen syndicate, 1919; geologist, geol. survey, Nigeria, 1920-29; ast. dir., 1929.

RAFFLES, MAJOR STAMFORD CRUZ, O.B.E. (Mily.), 1919.—B. 1885; ed. All Saints Sch., Bloxham, Royal Naval Academy, Gosport, and in Germany; 2nd lieut., 4th Suffolk regt., 1903; lieut., 1903; transfd., K.S.L.I., 1906; resig. coman., 1908; supt., chandu monopoly, Perak, 1913; seconded for mily. serv., Jan., 1915; lieut.,
3rd R.W.F., Mar., 1915; capt., Sept., 1915; staff offr., 3rd cls., R.F.C., 1917; staff offr., 2nd cls., R.A.F., 1918; tempy. major, 1918; transfd., unemployed list, R.A.F., Apr., 1919; resumed duty as supt., chandu monopoly, Perak, and supervisor, cust., Kinta, Dec., 1919; supervisor, cust., Selangor, Dec., 1920; dep. comsmr., trade and cust., F.M.S., Jan., 1921; cls. Ia, 1922; mem., joint F.M.S. and S.S. comte., to draw up a scheme for formn. of R.N.V.R. in Malaya, Apr., 1926; dep. comsmr., excise, F.M.S. in addn., Apr.-July, 1929; dep. comsmr., trade and cust., Selangor and Pahang, June, 1931.

RAIKES, H. R.—Ed. Tonbridge Schl., Dulwich Coll. and Balliol Coll., Oxford (Williams exhib.), Abbot Schol., 1911, final hon. schl. of nat. science (chemy.), class I, 1914; B.A., 1914; M.A., 1919; served European War, 1st Batt. The Buffs, R.F.C. and R.A.F., 1914-1919 (A.F.C.); fellow, Exeter Coll., Oxford, 1919-27; sub rector, 1924-27; demonstr. and treas., Balliol and Trinity Coll. laboratory, 1920-27; ch. instr., Oxford Univ. Air Squadron, 1925-27: wing commander, R.A.F.O. since 1926; prin., Univ. of Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, 1928; publs.—papers in Jnl.s. of Chem. Soc'y and Faraday Soc'y.

RAINSFORD, HUME FREDERICK.—B. 1902; ed. Dublin Univ.; B.A. and B.A.I. hons., civ. engnr., 1925; staff survr., Tanganyika Territory, 1927.

RAINSFORD, CAPT. RICHARD FREDERICK.—B. 1888; Natal pol., 1904-07, served Zulu Rebellion, 1906, (med.); B.S.A.P., 1907-08; inspr. E.A. Pol., 1910; asst. supt., 1914; commanded No. 1 Column, Turkhank Punitive Expdn., 1915 (deeps., A.G.S. med.) ; capt., 5th K.A.R., 1916; adjt. and staff offr. to O.C. troops, Jubaland, 1917-19 (deeps.); "1914-15" Star, Br. War and Victory med.; supdt., Kenya pol., 1923.

RAMBAUT, ARTHUR EDMUND, B.A.—B.1885; ed. Magd. Coll. Schl. and B.N.C., Oxford; 2nd cls. math. mods., 1905; 4th cls. bot., 1908; dipl. forestry, 1909; asst. con., forests, F.M.S., Nov., 1909; on mil. duty; 2nd lieut. North. Fus. (T.F.), 1915; lieut., 1916; temp. capt. 1916; served in France; intell. corps., 1917 (France, Belgium, Germany); rtnd. to F.M.S., Aug., 1919; dep. con., forests, Perak, South, Nov., 1926; ag. per. asst. to con., forests, Dec., 1927 and Aug., 1928; comsmr., forests, Jan., 1930.

RANASINHA, ARTHUR GODWIN, B.A. (Lond.)—B. 1898; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Jan., 1921; attd. to Kegalla Rath., Mar., 1921; attd., Jaffna kach., Oct., 1922; pol. mag., Pt. Pedro, Mar., 1923; ditto, Balapitiya, Nov., 1923; ditto, Jaffna, June, 1926; dist. judge Avisawella, Apr., 1928; ditto, Badulla, Jan., 1930.

RANKINE, SIR RICHARD SIMS DONKIN, K.C.M.G. (1932), C.M.G. (1919).—B. 1875; clk. treasury, Fiji, Feb., 1894; priv. sec. to Sir George O'Brien, Sept., 1897 to 1901; acted clk. to ex. coun. Sept., 1899 to Mar., 1900; apptd. acct. native taxes, treas., 1901; priv. sec. to Sir Henry Jackson, July, 1902; priv. sec. to Sir E. im Thurn, Oct., 1904; conf. sec., Jan., 1905; sec. to consul-gen. for W. Pacific; elk. of exec. coun.; ag. sec., W. Pacific high comsmr., June, 1905 to June, 1906, and from Nov., 1907 to Dec., 1908; asst. col. sec. and astt. recvr.-gen. Jan., 1909; recvr.-gen. and comsmr. of stamps, pres. of marine bd., mem. exec. and legis. couns., 1910; ag. col. sec., Nov., 1913 to Nov., 1914; gov'r's dep., in June, 1914; comsmr. of currency, Dec., 1914; ag. act.-gen. of immigrn. (conjoint), Mar., 1915; ag. col. sec., Aug., 1915 to May, 1916; gov'r's deputy, Aug., Oct., Dec., 1915; ag. col. sec. on various occasions, 1917-19; on sp. mission to India as personal rep. of the gov'r. in connection with emigrn. of Indians to Fiji, Oct., 1919 to June, 1920; ch. sec., Nyasaland Prot., July, 1920; ag. gov', on various occasions, 1921-24 and in 1926; ch. sec., Uganda, Aug., 1927; admstd. govt., June to Oct., 1928; Br. res., Zanzibar, 1929.

RANSOM, HON. ETHELBERT ALFRED.—B. 1868; ed. lower Hutt state schl., N.Z.; mem., N.Z., H. of R. since 1922; min. of pub. wks., 1928-30; min. of lands and comsmr., state forests, 1930; min., same offices, coalition min'y., 1931.

RANSOM, HERBERT CHARLES, O.B.E. (1923), M.B.E. (1920).—B. 1881; entd. crown ag't's off., May, 1901; asst. cashier, Mar., 1914; ag. head of appts. dept. and asst. sec., Jan., 1917; head of miscellaneous dept., Apr., 1919; dep. head, gen. dept., 14th Nov., 1921; sec., Dead Sea mineral reses comte., 1923; sec., Palestine currency bd., 1926-30; ch. clk. and head, gen. dept., Feb., 1930.

RANSOME, JOHN EDWARD GROFFREY.—B. 1891; ed. Bradfield Coll.; 3rd K.A.R., Oct., 1914-Mar., 1923; cadet, Tanganyika Territory, Mar., 1923; asst. dist. offr., Mar., 1925.

RAWSON, WALTER EDWARD.—B. 1870; ed. New Plymouth High Schl., N.Z.: barrister and solr.; judge, native land ct. and native appellate ct., N.Z., 1906; pres., Maori land bd., 1910; native trustee and east coast trust comsmr., 1921.

RAYMAN, LAZARUS.—B. 1889; ed. Manchester Gram. Schl. and Wadham Coll., Oxford; cadet, F.M.S., 1913; Brit. adviser's office, Kedah; asst. dist. offr., Pekan, Pahang, 1914-16; asst. dist. offr., Bentong, Pahang, on various occasions, 1916-19; asst. dist. offr., Ulu Selangor, 1917; asst. dist. offr., Ulu Selangor, 1919-21; on sp. duty as collr. of stamp duty, Mar., 1922; offr., cls. III, Nov., 1925; collr., estate duty, F.M.S., Oct., 1926; 2nd asst. sec. to gov't., Jan., 1927; ag. comsmr., lands and mines, Trengganu, Dec., 1929; cls. II, Nov., 1930; ag. finan. comsmr. and audr.-gen., Johore, Dec., 1930.

RAYMOND, LEONARD WILLIAM.—B. 1892; ed. Horwell Gr. Schl. and Dunheved Coll., Launceston; Royal Coll. Sci.; B.A. (Lond.), B.Sc. (Lond. 1912, hons. 1915), A.R.C.S. (1915), A.I.C. (1918); chem. offr., R.E., 1916; chem.-bactgts. with forces, Mesopotamia, 1917-20; asst. gov't. chem., agr. dept., Zanzibar, 1926; ag. gov't. chem., 1926; ag. asst. dir., agr., on various occasions, 1926-32; del., Imp. agr. conce., 1927.

RAYNE, MAJOR H., O.B.E. (1920), M.B.E. (Mily.)—B. and ed. N.Z.; N.Z. Contingents and R.F.A. in Anglo-Boer War, 1900-02; E. African pol., June, 1903; transport and polit. offr., Nandi and Sotik Expedns. (ment. in depts.), 1905-06; K.A.R., Sept., 1914 to Apr., 1919; asst. dist. comsmr., Br. E. Africa, Dec., 1914; seconded for mily. serv., German E. Africa, Jubaland and Turkana; offr. commdg. troops and administering Turkana, 1918 (ment. in depts.), M.C.; dist. comsmr., Somaliland, Apr., 1919; senr. supply and transport offr., in charge organisation of Somaliland expdn., 1919-20 (ment. in depts.); dist. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 1927.

READ, ALEXANDER LLEWELLYN.—B. 1877; ent. pub. serv., S. Australia, 1891; ch. sec.'s office, 1920; under sec., sec. to premier and clk., exec. coun., June, 1931.

READ, SIR HERBERT JAMES, K.C.M.G. (1918), C.B. (1914), C.M.G. (1907).—B. 1863; M.A., Brasenose Coll., Oxford; Ist class
math. mods., and 1st class math. finals; clk., higher div., W.O., Feb., 1887; 2nd class clk., C.O., Jan., 1889; asst. priv. sec. to Mr. Chamberlain, Sept., 1896; priv. sec. to Mr. (afterwards Sir E.) Wingfield, Feb., 1898; lst cls. clk., Oct., 1898; principal clk., Apr., 1905; British delegate at African liquor confce. at Brussels, 1899; one of the Brit. delegates on boundary comn. at Berlin for the settm. of Anglo-German frontier in E. Africa, 1906; one of the Brit. plenipotentiaries at African liquor confce. at Brussels, 1906; mem. of hon. man. comttee. of sleeping sickness bureau, 1908; chmn. of deptmtl. comttee. to enquire into W. African med. staff, 1909; visited E. Africa, 1911-12; sen. mem., C.O. delegation at Paris Peace Confce., 1919; asst. under-sec. of state, March, 1916; regiar. of the Order of Saint Michael and Saint George; gov., Mauritius, 1924 to 1930; hon. mem., managing comttee., Imp. Inst. of Entomology, 1931; hon. mem., managing comttee., Imp. Mycological Inst., 1932.

REAKES, CHARLES JOHN, C.B.E. (1919), M.R.C.V.S., Eng., Doctor of Vet. Science, Univ. of Melbourne.—B. 1885; vet. offr., N.Z. dept. of agr., 1897; asst. ch. vet., 1901; dir., live-stock divn., and dir. vet. services and remounts, N.Z. Defence Forces with rank of lieut.-col. (since col.), 1909; dir.-gen. agr. dept., 1918.

REAY, CAPT. GEORGE HENRY NORL, A.M.I.E.E.—B. 1889; asst. teleg. engr., F.M.S., Jan., 1914; war ser., 1915-19; elec. mpr., F.M.S., Nov., 1920; elec. engr., P.W.D., Singapore, July, 1922.

REDELINGHUYS, JOHANNES NICOLAS.—B. 1886; ed. Boys' High Sch., Wellington, C.P.; post and tel. asst., 1901; transf. to sec.'s office, dept. of posts and tels., Cape Town, 1909; senr. clk., 1920; ch. clk., 1924; asst. under sec., 1926; under sec. and asst. P.M.G., 1927.

RECE, C. MANSEL.—B. 1894; ed. Rossall Sch., and Magdalene Coll., Cambridge; called to bar, Inner Temple, 1921; prte. practice, Shanghai, 1921-26; res. mag., Zanzibar, 1927; ag. puisne judge, Apr.-May, 1929; crown coun., Uganda, 1930; ag. solr.-gen., Aug. to Feb., 1931 and May to Dec., 1931.

RECE, GERALD.—B. 1897; ed. Rugby Sch.; served in France with Sherwood Foresters, 1915-18; solr., sup. ct., England, 1921; adm. cadet, Kenya, 1925; dist. offr., 1927.

REED, E. A.—B. 1894; on milly. serv., Aug., 1914-Jan., 1918; temp. paper keeper, C.O. lib., 22nd Nov., 1920-15th Aug., 1924; estab. paper keeper (library attendant) after qual. exam., 16th Aug., 1924; cler. offr., 31st Oct., 1928.

REED, HATHORNE.—B. 1873; M.A., Cantab.; ed. Bath Coll. and Emmanuel Coll., Cambridge; called to the bar, Inner Temple, 1897; Western Circuit; lieut., S. African Constabulary, 1902-1908; 2nd mag., Zanzibar, Dec., 1908; 1st mag., Dec., 1910; ag. asst. judge, in 1910 and 1915-19; asst. judge, Sept., 1920; ag. chief judge and judge of prize ct., in 1919 and 1931-24; junr. puisne judge, Tanganyika Territory, May, 1925; judge, high ct., Nyasaland, 1927; author of "A Commentary on the Moneylenders' Act, 1900," and "A Commentary on the Police Offences Ordinance, 1902, of the Orange River Colony."

REED, HON. JOHN RANKEN, C.B.E. (1919).—B. 1864; ed. Gram. Sch., Auckland, N.Z., Victoria Coll., Jersey, and Clare Coll., Cambridge; judge, N.Z. sup. ct., 1921; pres., pri-ons bd., 1928; is judge advoc.-gen., N.Z. Defence Forces, with rank of colonel.

REES, LEWIS CHARLES MORRIS PARKER.—B. 1876; ed. Kingston Coll., Yeovil and Merchant Venturers Tech. Coll., Bristol; art. pupil to Messrs. Foster and La Trobe, archs. and survs., Bristol, 1892; asst. to boro. engrnr., Islington, 1897; ch. asst. borough engrnr., Margate, 1900; priv. land surveyor, P.W.D., Hong Kong, 1902; salaried, squatters' bd., 1905; aspt., crown lands and survs., 1922.

REES-DAVIES, SIR WM., KT. BACH. (1913).—B. 1863; ed. Eton and Trin. Hall, Camb.; B.A., 1888; called to bar (Inner Temp.), 1887; went South Wales circuit; J.P. and dep. lieut. Pembrokeshire; J.P. for Haverfordwest; M.P. for Pembrokeshire, 1892-8; priv. sec. to the late Rt. Hon. Sir W. V. Harcourt when chancellor of exchequer, 1893-5, and afterwards from 1895-8; atty.-gen., Bahamas, 1897; administered the govt., 1901; ag. ch. just., 1902; King's advocate, Cyprus, Oct., 1902; atty.-gen., Hong Kong, 1906; K.C., 1908; ag. ch. just., 1909-10; ch. just., Hong Kong, 1912; chmn. of gen. mily. serv. tribunal, 1918; chmn., pub. serv. comn., Hong Kong, 1919; chmn., exec. comttee. on the visit of H.R.H. The Prince of Wales, 1922; ret., 1924.

REGNARD, MAJOR LOUIS FERDINAND.—B. 1888; ed. R. Coll., Mauritius, Imp. Coll. of Sci. and Technology and McGill Univ. (B.Sc.); 2nd lieut., R.E., Nov., 1914; war. serv., France, Belgium and Palestine, 1914-20; major, R.E., 1918-20; regular army R. O. of asst. D.P.W. and surveys, Mauritius, 1921; D.P.W., 1926; M.L.C.

REID, C. B. B., M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.).—Capt., R.A.M.C., 1917-19; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Feb., 1919.

REID, FREDERICK MURRAY.—B. 1875; inspr., schls., Basutoland, Oct., 1914; senr. inspr., ashl., 1927.

REID, HAROLD WALLACE, B.Sc.—B. 1897; dep. inspr., mines, Trinidad, Sept., 1927.

REILLY, ROBERT O'MALLEY.—Sub-inspr., Bechuanaland Prot. police, 1904; passed Cape civ. ser. lower law exam., 1909; ag. asst. res. mag., 1912; inspr., Apr., 1914; ag. res. mag., 1914; res. mag., 1921; passed 3rd grade Seswana exam., 1922; asst. res. comntr., Oct., 1931; ag. res. comntr., April to Oct., 1932.

REIMERS, EDMUND.—B. 1881; archivist and librarian, Ceylon, Oct., 1921.

REJAS, FELIX.—B. 1856; entd. civ. ser., Trinidad, Feb., 1887; warden, July, 1912.

RENNIE, GILBERT MCCALL, M.C., M.A. (Glas.).—B. 1895; on milly. serv., July, 1915; cadet, Ceylon, Apr., 1920; attd. to Anuradhapura Kachcheri, June, 1920; attd. to N'Ella Kachcheri, Nov., 1920; office asst. to govt. agt. E. Prov., Nov., 1921; pol. mag., Dambagamuwa, Dec., 1923; ditto, Chilaw, Mar., 1924; addnl. dist. judge, Mannar and Mullaitivu, Dec., 1923; office asst. to dir., med. and sanry. services, Apr., 1926; sec., min. for health, July, 1931.

RENTON, SIR ALEXANDER WOOD, G.C.M.G. (1930), K.C.M.G. (1925), KT. BACH. (1915); M.A., LL.B. (honours), Edin., K.C.—Forensic prizeman; Lord Rector's essay prizeman; Bacon scholar, Gray's Inn, 1882; bencher, Gray's Inn, 1917; b. 1861; called to the bar, 1886; puisne judge, Mauritius, Aug., 1901; chmn., local comttee. of soc. of comp. legis., 1902; chmn. of mountain reserves comn., 1903-4; ag. procureur and advocato-gen., Aug., 1904; puisne judge, Ceylon, Aug., 1905; received thanks of S. of S. for drafting rules of sup. ct. of Mauritius, 1904; mem. of comttee. apptd. in 1912 to prepare new code of civil procedure, Ceylon; ag. chief
DOMINIONS OFFICE AND COLONIAL OFFICE LIST.

ust., Ceylon, May, 1913; chief just., Ceylon, Aug., 1914; chmn., police inquiry comsn., Sept., 1915; chmn. of coman. of inquiry into certain cases of shooting during Ceylon riots, 1915; ret., 25th July, 1918; on special mission to Nigeria and G. Coast as to war bonus, Sept., 1918 (recd. thanks of S. of S.); went to Egypt at request of F.O., Feb., 1919, and prepared draft Code of Criminal Procedure for Unified Tribunals; chmn., comsn. of enquiry, Upper Egypt train murders; vice-pres., riots indemnities coman., Oct., 1919; chmn., Ceylon salaries coman., June, 1921; chmn., compensation (Ireland) coman., Feb., 1923; K.C., 12th Oct., 1923; author of "Wood Renton on Lunacy"; joint author of first edition of "Edmunds on Patents"; editor of Law Journal; editor of "Encyclopedia of the Laws of England"; editor of "The English Reports"; joint editor of 2nd edition of "Burge on Colonial and Foreign Laws."

RENWICK, HENRY LANGDON.—B. 1898; London Rifle Brig., Apr., 1916; attd. gen. staff, W.O., 1919; asst. clk. to H.M.T.C. in E. Africa, Dec., 1919; asst. imigrn. and embarkation offr., Mombasa, July, 1920; asst. cust. dept., Zanzibar, Dec., 1920; imigrn., offr., Aug., 1921; ag. asst. compt., cust., for various periods, 1923-32; ag. asst. treas., May, 1932; aviation control offr., Aug., 1932.

RETIEF, D. J., B.A.—B. 1882; ed. Victoria Coll., Stellenbosch; prin., Boshof, 1913; prin., Winburg, 1921; inspr. of schls., O.F.S., 1927.

REX, MARCUS.—B. 1886; ed. Highgate and Trin. Coll., Camb. (exhib.), B.A., 1908; cadet, F.M.S., 1910; asst. sec. to res., Perak, 1912 and 1915; asst. dist. offr., K. Kangsar, 1913; supk., chandu monopoly, Sel., N.S. and Pahang, 1917; dist. offr., Raub, 1919; mag., K. Lumpur, June, 1921, sec., retrenchment coman., in addition, Feb., 1922; dep. contr. of rubber expts., in addition, Oct., 1922; offr., cls. III., Nov., 1923; ag. finan. advr., Johore, 1924; ag. finan. advr. and treas., F.M.S., Nov., 1927; finan. advr. and treas., F.M.S., Jan., 1932.

REY, CHARLES FERNAND, C.M.G. (1932)—B. 1877; W. Africa, 1900; joined B. of T. 1900; sec. to China Tariff coman., 1902; to Imp. Inst. Advisory Comte. and Imp. Inst. Trustees, 1903; to All Red Route Comtes., 1904; Roumanian Treaty Negotiations, 1905; mission to Constantinople and Sofia, 1906; Swiss Treaty negotiations, 1906; gen. man., lab. exchange and unemployment insurance, 1909; asst. gen. sec., min. of munitions 1916; dir., employment dept., B. of T., 1917; dir.-gen., national lab. supply, miny. of national service, 1918; chmn. and Br. rep., Inter-Allied coman., Rotterdam, for food supply to Germany; seconded for serv. in Abyssinia, 1919; further journeys to Abyssinia, 1922-3, 1925-6, 1926-7; unemployment grants comitee, 1920-29; asst. res. coman., Bechuanaland Prot., Oct., 1929; res. coman., June, 1930; F.R.G.S., commdr., Order of the Star of Ethiopia; author of "Unconquered Abyssinia as it is today," 1923; "In the country of the Blue Nile," 1927; "The Romance of the Portuguese in Abyssinia," 1929; "The Lady or the Leopard," 1929; contributions to the Royal Geographical Jnl. and the Jnl. of the African Society.

REYNOLDS, A. E.—B. 1881; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to the C.O., Aug., 1900; conf. clk., 1st Jan., 1918.

RHODES, ALEX LEOPOLD.—B. 1884; gen. foreman, govt. printing and stationery dept., Trinidad 1921; typography instr., bd. of indus. training, 1922; mem., bd. indus. training, 1923; govt. printer, 1925.

RHODES, HON. E. N., P.C. (Can.), K.C., B.A., LL.B., D.C.L.—B. 1877; ed. Amherst Acad., Acadia Univ. and Dalhousie Univ.; apptd. K.C., Nova Scotia, May, 1916; 1st el. to H. of C. Canada at g.e., 1908; el. dep. speaker, H. of C., Feb., 1916; speaker, 1917; re-el. Mar., 1918; el. to legis., N.S., 1925; prov. premier and prov. sec., 1925; re-el. at g.e., 1928; joined Dominion cabinet of Bennett adminstr., as min. of fisheries, Aug. 1930.

RHODES, HON. SIR ROBERT HEATON, M.L.C. (1925), K.C.V.O. (1927), K.B.E. (1920).—B. 1861; B.A. Oxford; entd. New Zealand parlmt., 1899; served in S.
